Tafsir of Surah an-Nahl

It is a Meccan surah.

* *

Allah, exalted is He, informs of the drawing near and approach of the Hour, expressing it in the past tense, which indicates its certainty and that it will occur without doubt, as He said: ﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness, turning away﴾ [al-Anbiya: 1], and He said: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1].

And His saying: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾ means: what is far has come near, so do not seek to hasten it.

The pronoun may refer to Allah, and it may refer to the punishment; both meanings are interrelated, as Allah said: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment. Were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. It will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive. They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will encompass the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 53-54].

Al-Dahhak, in his interpretation of this verse, took a strange position: he said, regarding His saying ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾, that it means His obligations and His limits.

Ibn Jarir refuted him, saying: "We know of no one who hastened to the obligations and the laws before they existed, unlike the punishment, for they hastened to it before it occurred, out of disbelief and mockery."

I say: As Allah said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error﴾ [ash-Shura: 18].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Yahya ibn Adam, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the client of al-Mughira ibn Shu'bah, from Ka'b ibn Alqamah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hujayrah, from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Near the Hour, a black cloud will appear to you from the west, like a shield. It will keep rising in the sky, then a caller will call out from it: 'O people!' So the people will turn to one another, saying: 'Did you hear?' Some of them will say: 'Yes,' and some will doubt. Then the caller will call a second time: 'O people!' So the people will say to one another: 'Did you hear?' And they will say: 'Yes.' Then he will call a third time: 'O people, the command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, two men will be spreading a garment, but they will never fold it up; and a man will be drawing water for his pool, but he will never give any of it to drink; and a man will be milking his she-camel, but he will never drink it.' He said: 'And the people will be occupied.'"

[It was related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/539): Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Affan related to us, Yahya ibn Adam related to us with it, and he said: "Its chain is sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." It was also related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/325): al-Husayn al-Tustari related to us, Abu Kurayb related to us, Yahya ibn Adam related to us with it. Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (4/382): "Al-Tabarani related it with a good chain whose narrators are trustworthy and well known."]

Then He, exalted is He, declared Himself free from their associating others with Him, and their worshipping alongside Him whatever else is among idols and rivals, exalted and sanctified far above that. These are the ones who deny the Hour. So He said: ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate with Him﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit﴾, meaning with the revelation (wahy), as He says: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

* *

And His saying: ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ refers to the prophets, as He says: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124], and He says: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾ [al-Hajj: 75], and He says: ﴿He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that he may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. "Whose is the dominion today?" "It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer"﴾ [Ghafir: 15-16].

* *

And His saying: ﴿that warn﴾ means: that they may warn ﴿that there is no god except Me﴾ [as He says: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god except Me﴾] ﴿so fear Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. And He says in this verse: ﴿so fear Me﴾, meaning: fear My punishment, for whoever opposes My command and worships other than Me.

He, the Exalted, informs about His creation of the upper world, which is the heavens, and the lower world, which is the earth and what it contains. He also informs that this was created with truth, not in vain. Rather, ﴿that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did and recompense those who did good with the best reward﴾ [An-Najm: 31].

Then He declared Himself free of the polytheism of those who worship others besides Him, [such as the idols, which create nothing while they themselves are created. How, then, is it fitting that anything else should be worshipped along with Him?] He alone is the sole Creator, with no partner. Therefore, He alone deserves to be worshipped, with no partner.

Then He drew attention to the creation of the human species ﴿from a drop of fluid﴾, meaning weak and despised. When he grew strong and advanced, he began to dispute with his Lord, the Exalted, to deny Him, and to wage war against His messengers. Yet he was only created to be a servant, not an adversary, as the Exalted said: ﴿And it is He who created from water a human being and made him [a lineage of] descent and marriage. And your Lord is ever Powerful. And they worship other than Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper [of Satan] against his Lord﴾ [Al-Furqan: 54–55]. And He said: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop of fluid, and then he is an open adversary? And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is, of all creation, Knowing"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77–79].

In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Majah from Bisr ibn Jahhash, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spat into his palm and then said: "Allah says: 'O son of Adam, how can you incapacitate Me when I created you from something like this? When I had perfected you and made you balanced, you walked between your two cloaks while the earth was [made] smooth for you. Then you gathered [wealth] and withheld [it]. When the soul reached the throat, you said: "I will give charity." But how can there be a time for charity now?'"

[Al-Musnad (4/210) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2707. Al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (2/365): "Its chain is sound; its narrators are trustworthy. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad from the hadith of Bisr, and its origin is in the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah."]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 16, verses 5–7:

Allah blesses His servants with what He created for them of the livestock (al-an'am), namely camels, cattle and sheep, which He detailed in Surah al-An'am into eight pairs, and with the benefits and advantages they contain: from their wool, their fleece and their hair they make clothing and bedding, and from their milk they drink, and they eat of their young. And there is for them in them beauty (al-jamal), which is adornment. Therefore He said: ﴿And for you in them is beauty when you bring them back in the evening﴾, which is the time of their return in the afternoon from pasture, when their flanks are fullest, their udders most abundant and their humps highest. ﴿And when you send them out to pasture﴾, i.e., in the morning when you send them forth to pasture.

﴿And they carry your loads﴾, which are the heavy burdens that you cannot move or carry, ﴿to a land you could not reach except with great hardship to yourselves﴾. This is for Hajj, 'Umrah, military campaigns, trade and what runs in their course; you use them in various kinds of use, such as riding and carrying, as He said: ﴿And indeed for you in livestock is a lesson. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are many benefits, and from them you eat, and upon them and upon ships you are carried﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 21–22]. He also said: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the livestock that you may ride some of them and eat from them, and for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need within your breasts, and upon them and upon ships you are carried. And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾ [Ghafir: 79–81]. Therefore, after enumerating these favours, He said here: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾, i.e., your Lord who facilitated these livestock for you and subjected them to you, as He said: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made livestock, so they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71–72]. And He said: ﴿And made for you of ships and livestock that which you ride, that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are settled upon them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have otherwise subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 12–14].

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿For you in them is warmth (dif')﴾, i.e., clothing, and "benefits" are what you derive benefit from of foods and drinks.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Israil informed us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Warmth and benefits﴾ — the offspring of every animal.

Mujahid said: ﴿For you in them is warmth﴾ — he said: clothing that is woven, and benefits that are ridden, and meat and milk.

Qatadah said: ﴿Warmth and benefits﴾ — he means: for you in them is clothing, and benefit, and sustenance.

Similarly, others among the exegetes said, in closely similar wording.

This is another category of what Allah, exalted is He, created for His servants, by which He bestows favour upon them: horses, mules and donkeys, which He made for riding and for adornment. Riding is the greatest of their purposes. Because He separated them from the livestock (al-an'am) and mentioned them individually, scholars who held that horse meat is forbidden used this as evidence for their position, among them the Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him,[[In manuscripts F and A: "may Allah have mercy on him."]] and those jurists who agreed with him, because He linked horses with mules and donkeys, and those are forbidden, as the Prophetic Sunnah (the body of the Prophet's traditions) has established, and most scholars hold this view.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated: Ya'qub told me, Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, Hisham al-Dastuwa'i informed us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir told us, from the mawla (freedman) of Nafi' ibn 'Alqamah, that Ibn 'Abbas disliked the eating of horse, mule and donkey meat, and he would say: Allah said: ﴿And the cattle, He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat﴾, so these are for eating; ﴿And horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride﴾, so these are for riding.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/57).]]

Similarly, it has been narrated through the chain of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of this. Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah[[In manuscripts T, F and A: "'Uyaynah."]] likewise said the same, may Allah be pleased with him.[[In manuscript T: "may Allah have mercy on him."]] They also relied on a hadith that Imam Ahmad related in his Musnad:

Yazid ibn 'Abd Rabbih told us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid told us, Thawr ibn Yazid told us, from Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, from his father, from his grandfather, from Khalid ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the eating of the meat of horses, mules and donkeys.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also transmitted it from the hadith of Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Miqdam, and there is criticism concerning it, with this wording.[[Al-Musnad (4/89); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3790); Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/202); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3198).]]

Ahmad also related it by another route, more detailed than this and more explicit, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik told us, Muhammad ibn Harb told us, Sulayman ibn Salim told us, from Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Miqdam, from his grandfather al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, who said: We campaigned with Khalid ibn al-Walid in the summer raid (al-sa'ifah), and our companions longed for meat, so they asked me for a mare (ramakah). I gave it to them and they tied it up,[[In manuscript T: "fa-gharim" (they craved).]] and I said: Stay where you are until I go to Khalid and ask him. I went to him and asked him, and he said: We campaigned with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the battle of Khaybar, and the people hastened to the orchards of the Jews. He ordered me to call out: "Gather for prayer, and none will enter Paradise except a Muslim." Then he said: "O people, you have hastened to the orchards of the Jews. Indeed, the property of those under covenant is not lawful except by its right. It is forbidden for you to eat the flesh of domestic donkeys, their horses and their mules, and every animal with fangs of the beasts of prey, and every bird with talons."[[In manuscript F: "la yahillu" (is not lawful).]][[In manuscripts T and F: "al-hummar" (the donkeys).]][[Al-Musnad (4/89).]]

The ramakah is the hijrah (a mare, a female horse). Their saying "habalu-ha" means they tied her with a rope in order to slaughter her. The hazair (orchards) are the gardens near inhabited areas.

It seems that this action occurred after they had given the covenant and had made a sharecropping arrangement with them (al-shatr), and Allah knows best.

If this hadith were sound, it would be explicit in forbidding the meat of horses. But it cannot withstand what is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the meat of domestic donkeys and permitted the meat of horses.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4219, 5524); Sahih Muslim, no. (1941).]]

Ahmad and Abu Dawud also related it by two chains, each of which meets the condition of Muslim, from Jabir, who said: On the day of Khaybar we slaughtered horses, mules and donkeys, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from mules and donkeys, but did not forbid us from horses.[[Al-Musnad (3/356); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3789).]]

In Sahih Muslim, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with both of them, she said: We slaughtered a horse during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ate it while we were in Madinah.[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1942).]]

These are more explicit, stronger and more authentic, and to this view the majority of scholars went: Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and their followers, and most of the early generations (al-salaf) and later ones (al-khalaf). And Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ibn Jurayj told us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The horses were wild, and Allah made them tame for Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon them both.

Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned in his Isra'iliyyat (narratives traced to Israelite sources): that Allah created horses from the south wind. And Allah knows best.

The text indicates the permissibility of riding these animals, among them mules. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was presented with a mule, and he used to ride it, even though he had forbidden the mating of donkeys with horses, lest offspring be cut off.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd told me, 'Umar of the family of Hudhayfah told us, from al-Sha'bi, from Dahiyah al-Kalbi, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not mount a donkey on a mare for you, so that she bears you a mule that you may ride?" He said: "Only those who do not know do that."[[Al-Musnad (4/311).]]

When He, exalted is He, mentioned among the animals those that are ridden upon and used for travel along sensory paths, He drew attention to the spiritual, religious paths. In the Qur'an, it often happens that the discourse passes from sensory matters to beneficial spiritual and religious matters, as when He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾ [al-Baqarah: 197], and He said: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment; but the clothing of piety, that is best﴾ [al-A'raf: 26].

When He mentioned in this surah the animals, including the livestock and others, which they ride and by which they reach a need that is in their breasts, and which carry their burdens to distant lands and places and arduous journeys, He began to mention the paths that people take to Him. He explained that among these paths, only those which lead to Him are the true ones, so He said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, as He said: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am: 153], and He said: ﴿This is a path upon Me, straight﴾ [al-Hijr: 41].

Mujahid said, regarding His saying ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾: it is the path of truth that leads to Allah.

As-Suddi said, regarding ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾: it is Islam.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾: he said: "And upon Allah is the clarification," meaning: the clarifying of guidance and misguidance.

Similarly, Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from him, and Qatadah and ad-Dahhak also said similarly. However, the statement of Mujahid here is stronger in terms of context, because He, exalted is He, informed that there are paths traversed toward Him, and none of them reaches Him except the path of truth, which is the path He legislated and approved, while whatever else is blocked off, and the deeds in it are rejected. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among them is the deviating one﴾, meaning: swerving, inclining, and turning away from the truth.

Ibn Abbas and others said: these are the various paths and the divergent opinions and desires, such as Judaism, Christianity, and Zoroastrianism. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And among you is the deviating one."

Then He informed that all of that occurs by His power and will, so He said: ﴿And if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾, as He said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on the earth would have believed, all of them entirely﴾ [Yunus: 99], and He said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community, but they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy; and for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"﴾ [Hud: 118-119].

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 16, verses 14–18:

He (Exalted is He) informs of His subjugating the sea with its tumultuous waves, and bestows favour upon His servants by making it submissive to them, facilitating their riding upon it, creating fish and aquatic animals in it, and permitting His servants to eat its meat, both alive and dead, in a state of lawfulness and while in ihram (the sacred state of pilgrimage). He also mentions the pearls and precious gems He creates in it, and His making it easy for the servants to extract them from its depths as adornment that they wear, and His subjugating the sea for the carrying of ships that plough through it, meaning: they cut through it (*tamkhuru*).

It was also said: they plough through the winds. Both meanings are correct, with its *juju'ihā*, which is its prow, the raised front part, which guided the servants to the craft of building them and showed them how to do so, as an inheritance from their father Noah (peace be upon him). He was the first to ride ships, and it was he who taught their construction. Then people took it from him generation after generation and age after age, travelling from region to region, from land to land, and from territory to territory, bringing what is here to there and what is there to here. Therefore He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾, meaning: His blessings and His kindness.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his *Musnad*: I found in my book, from Muhammad ibn Mu'awiya al-Baghdadi: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn [Umar, from] Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayra [raising it to the Prophet ﷺ], who said: Allah spoke to this western sea and spoke to the eastern sea. He said to the western sea: "I am carrying in you some of My servants; how will you treat them?" It said: "I will drown them." He said: "Your might is in your regions; I will carry them upon my hands, and I forbid you the ornaments and the game." Then He spoke to this eastern sea and said: "I am carrying in you some of My servants; what will you do with them?" It said: "I will carry them upon my hands, and I will be for them like a mother to her child." So He rewarded it with the ornaments and the game.

Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know anyone who narrated it from Suhayl except Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, and he is weak in narration (*munkar al-hadith*). Suhayl also narrated it from al-Nu'man ibn Abi Ayyash, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, as a statement of his own (*mawquf*).

Then Allah (Exalted is He) mentioned the earth and what He placed in it of towering mountains and firmly fixed hills, so that the earth would be steady and not sway, meaning: it would not shake with what is upon it of living creatures, and thus life would not be pleasant for them. Therefore He said: ﴿And the mountains He set firmly﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 32].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "When the earth was created, it was swaying, so they (the angels) said: 'This will not keep anyone steady on its back.' In the morning the mountains had been created, and the angels did not know what the mountains were created from."

Sa'id narrated from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Qays ibn Ubada: When Allah (Exalted is He) created the earth, it began to quake, so the angels said: "This will not keep anyone steady on its back." It awoke in the morning with its mountains upon it.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abd Allah ibn Habib, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When Allah created the earth, it shook and said: "O Lord, will You make the children of Adam act upon me with sins and place filth upon me?" He said: "So Allah set firm in it the mountains that you see and that you do not see, and its steadiness became like flesh that quivers."

* *

His saying ﴿and rivers and roads﴾: meaning, He placed in it rivers flowing from one place to another, as provision for the servants. Water springs forth in one place and is provision for the people of another place. It cuts through the lands, the deserts and the wastelands, pierces the mountains and the hills, and reaches the town that has been made subservient to its people. They flow across the earth to the right and to the left, south and north, east and west, between small and large (rivers). There are valleys that flow at times and stop at other times, and some springs and some flows, some strong in their course and some slow, according to what He willed and decreed, subjected and facilitated. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Likewise He placed in it roads, meaning: paths along which one travels from land to land. Indeed, He (Exalted is He) cuts through the mountain so that between its two sides there is a passage and a way, as He said: ﴿And We have made in it wide roads as paths﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 31].

* *

His saying ﴿and landmarks﴾: meaning, signs from great mountains and small hills and the like, by which travellers by land and sea are guided when they lose their way, by day.

* *

His saying ﴿and by the star they are guided﴾: meaning, in the darkness of the night. Ibn Abbas said this.

It is related from Malik regarding His saying ﴿and landmarks﴾ that they said: these are the stars, and they are the mountains.

Then Allah (Exalted is He) said, drawing attention to His greatness and that worship is fitting only for Him, to the exclusion of all else besides Him of idols, which create nothing but are themselves created: ﴿Then is One who creates like one who does not create? Will you not remember?﴾

Then He drew their attention to the abundance of His blessings upon them and His kindness toward them, saying: ﴿And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: He overlooks your shortcomings. Were He to demand from you thanks for all His blessings, you would be unable to fulfil that. Were He to command you to do so, you would be weak and would abandon it. Were He to punish you, He would be punishing you while not being unjust to you. But He is Forgiving and Merciful; He forgives much and rewards the little.

Ibn Jarir said: He means: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward what has come from you of shortcoming in thanking Him for some of it, if you repent and turn back to His obedience and to following what pleases Him; ﴿Merciful﴾ to you, in that He does not punish you after your turning back and repentance.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abd Allah ibn Habib, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When Allah created the earth, it shook and said: "O Lord, will You make the children of Adam act upon me with sins and place filth upon me?" * *

His saying ﴿and rivers and roads﴾: meaning, He placed in it rivers flowing from one place to another, as provision for the servants. Water springs forth in one place and is provision for the people of another place. They flow across the earth to the right and to the left, south and north, east and west, between small and large (rivers). There are valleys that flow at times and stop at other times, and some springs and some flows, some strong in their course and some slow, according to what He willed and decreed, subjected and facilitated. * *

His saying ﴿and landmarks﴾: meaning, signs from great mountains and small hills and the like, by which travellers by land and sea are guided when they lose their way, by day.

* *

* *

The Exalted says: When it is said to these deniers, ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?"﴾, they turn away from answering and say: ﴿"Tales of the former peoples."﴾ That is, He has sent down nothing; rather, what is recited to us is merely the tales of the former peoples, meaning that it is taken from the books of earlier generations. As the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ [al-Furqan: 5]. That is, they fabricate against the Messenger and make various, contradictory statements about him, all of which are false, as the Exalted said: ﴿See how they have coined comparisons for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾ [al-Furqan: 9]. This is because everyone who departs from the truth, whatever he says, is in error. They used to say: "He is a sorcerer, a poet, a soothsayer, and a madman." Then their affair settled on what their shaykh, the one known as al-Waḥid, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, devised for them, when ﴿he reflected and calculated; so may he be destroyed, how he calculated! Again, may he be destroyed, how he calculated! Then he looked, then he frowned and scowled, then he turned away and was arrogant, and said: "This is nothing but magic transmitted from others."﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 18–24]. That is, it is transmitted and related. So they dispersed from his statement and opinion. May Allah disfigure them.

The Exalted said: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge.﴾ That is, We only decreed for them that they should say this, so that they would bear their own burdens and some of the burdens of those who follow them and agree with them. That is, the sin of their own misguidance will fall upon them, along with the sin of leading others astray and of those people following them. As has come in the hadith: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing their rewards in the least; and whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing their sins in the least."

And the Exalted said: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13].

Others said: "This is by way of parable, to nullify what those who disbelieved in Allah and associated others with Him in worship had done, just as Nuh, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And they plotted a great plot﴾ [Nuh: 22], meaning: they schemed to lead people astray by every means and inclined them toward their polytheism by every method, just as their followers will say to them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Nay, but it was your plotting by night and day, when you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him﴾ [Saba': 33], and so on."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So Allah came at their building from its foundations﴾, meaning: He uprooted it from its base and nullified their work, and its roots (wa-asluha) were as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64].

* *

And His words: ﴿So Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and cast terror into their hearts; they destroy their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O you with insight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2].

Here He said: ﴿So Allah came at their building from its foundations, and the roof fell down upon them from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them﴾

That is: He will expose their disgrace and what their inner thoughts had concealed, making it public, just as He said: ﴿The Day when secrets are tested﴾ [al-Tariq: 9], meaning: they will be made manifest and become known. This is as in the two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For every treacherous person a banner will be raised on the Day of Resurrection at his backside, according to the extent of his treachery, and it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3188) and Sahih Muslim no. (1735)].

Likewise, these people: what they used to conceal of plotting will be shown to the people, and Allah will disgrace them before all creation. The Lord, blessed and exalted, will say to them, rebuking and reproaching them: ﴿Where are My associates about whom you used to contend?﴾, meaning: you used to fight and oppose on their behalf. That is: where are they now concerning your help and deliverance here? ﴿Can they help you or help themselves?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 93], ﴿So he will have no power nor any helper﴾ [al-Tariq: 10]. When the proof is established against them, the evidence is upheld, the word is fulfilled against them, and they are silenced from making excuses, when there is no escape, ﴿those who were given knowledge will say﴾ — and they are the leaders in this world and the Hereafter, and the ones who inform about the truth in this world and the Hereafter — so they will say at that time: ﴿Indeed, disgrace today and evil are upon the disbelievers﴾, meaning: disgrace and punishment today encompass those who disbelieved in Allah and associated with Him that which neither harms nor benefits him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verses 28–29:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the state of the polytheists, who wronged themselves, at the time of their death (ihtidar) and when the angels come to them to seize their souls: ﴿Then they will offer submission﴾, that is, they will display hearing, obedience and submission, saying: ﴿"We did not used to do any evil."﴾ Just as they will say on the Day of Return (al-Ma'ad): ﴿"By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ [Al-An'am: 23] ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him just as they swear to you﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 18].

Allah says, refuting them for their statement: ﴿"Yes! Indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do. So enter the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein. And wretched is the residence of the arrogant."﴾ [In one manuscript: "fa-bi'sa".] That is: how wretched is the resting place, the station and the abode of humiliation, for one who was arrogant toward the signs of Allah and toward following His messengers.

They enter Hell from the day of their death with their souls, and its heat and scorching winds reach their bodies in their graves. When the Day of Resurrection comes, their souls are returned into their bodies and they abide eternally in the Fire of Hell: ﴿Its punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given death therein, nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ [Fatir: 36], as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the Day the Hour is established, [it will be said], "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verses 35–37:

Allah, exalted is He, tells of the delusion of the polytheists in the shirk they were engaged in, and of their excuses, arguing from divine decree (al-qadar), in their saying: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have declared anything unlawful apart from Him.﴾ That is, [they declared unlawful] of the baheerah, the sawaa'ib, the waseelah and other things, which they had innovated and invented of their own accord, [for] which Allah had not sent down any authority.

The substance of their statement is: if Allah were averse to what we do, He would have denied it to us by punishment, and would not have empowered us to do it. Allah replied, refuting their doubt: ﴿So upon the Messengers is only the clear delivery.﴾ That is, the matter is not as you claim, that He did not disapprove of it or forbid it; rather He has denounced it to you in the strongest terms and forbidden it to you in the most emphatic way. He sent a Messenger to every nation, that is, to every generation of people and every group, and all of them call to the worship of Allah and forbid the worship of anything other than Him: ﴿Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut (false deities).﴾ Allah has continued to send Messengers to people with this message since shirk arose among the children of Adam, beginning with the people of Nuh, to whom Nuh was sent, and he was the first Messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth, until He sealed them with Muhammad ﷺ, whose call reached mankind and jinn in the east and the west. All of them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you any Messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 25] And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our Messengers: Did We appoint deities to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 45] And Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a Messenger, [saying], Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut.﴾ So how can any polytheist, after this, say: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him﴾? His legislative will (al-mashi'ah al-shar'iyyah) is therefore negated, because He forbade them from that through the tongues of His Messengers. As for His universal will (al-mashi'ah al-kawniyyah), which is His empowering them to do so by decree (qadar), they have no proof in it, because Allah created the Fire and its people from the devils and the disbelievers, and He does not approve of disbelief for His servants; and for Him in that is a conclusive proof and a decisive wisdom.

Then Allah the Exalted has informed that He denounced them and denied them by punishment in this world after the warning of the Messengers. Therefore He said: ﴿Among them are those whom Allah guided, and among them are those upon whom misguidance was justly decreed. So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ That is, ask about what befell those who opposed the Messengers and denied the truth, how ﴿Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar [consequences].﴾ [Muhammad: 10] ﴿And those before them denied, so how was My denunciation?﴾ [al-Mulk: 18]

Then Allah the Exalted informed His Messenger ﷺ that his eagerness for their guidance would not benefit them, if Allah had willed to lead them astray, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever Allah intends to test, you cannot avail him anything from Allah.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41] And Nuh said to his people: ﴿And my advice will not benefit you if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to mislead you.﴾ [Hud: 34] And He said in this noble verse: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those who mislead.⁠﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever Allah misguides, there is no guide for him, and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [al-A'raf: 186] And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96–97]

As for His saying ﴿indeed Allah﴾, that is, His affair and command is that whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be; therefore He said: ﴿does not guide those who mislead﴾, that is, whom He has led astray, so who can guide him after Allah? That is, no one. ﴿And they have no helpers﴾, that is, who could rescue them from His punishment and His bonds. ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verses 35–37:

The substance of their statement is: if Allah were averse to what we do, He would have denied it to us by punishment, and would not have empowered us to do it. Allah replied, refuting their doubt: ﴿So upon the Messengers is only the clear delivery.﴾ That is, the matter is not as you claim, that He did not disapprove of it or forbid it; rather He has denounced it to you in the strongest terms and forbidden it to you in the most emphatic way. He sent a Messenger to every nation, that is, to every generation of people and every group, and all of them call to the worship of Allah and forbid the worship of anything other than Him: ﴿Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut (false deities).﴾ Allah has continued to send Messengers to people with this message since shirk arose among the children of Adam, beginning with the people of Nuh, to whom Nuh was sent, and he was the first Messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth, until He sealed them with Muhammad ﷺ, whose call reached mankind and jinn in the east and the west. All of them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you any Messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 25] And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our Messengers: Did We appoint deities to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 45] And Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a Messenger, [saying], Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut.﴾ So how can any polytheist, after this, say: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him﴾? His legislative will (al-mashi'ah al-shar'iyyah) is therefore negated, because He forbade them from that through the tongues of His Messengers. As for His universal will (al-mashi'ah al-kawniyyah), which is His empowering them to do so by decree (qadar), they have no proof in it, because Allah created the Fire and its people from the devils and the disbelievers, and He does not approve of disbelief for His servants; and for Him in that is a conclusive proof and a decisive wisdom.

Then Allah the Exalted has informed that He denounced them and denied them by punishment in this world after the warning of the Messengers. Therefore He said: ﴿Among them are those whom Allah guided, and among them are those upon whom misguidance was justly decreed. So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ That is, ask about what befell those who opposed the Messengers and denied the truth, how ﴿Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar [consequences].﴾ [Muhammad: 10] ﴿And those before them denied, so how was My denunciation?﴾ [al-Mulk: 18]

As for His saying ﴿indeed Allah﴾, that is, His affair and command is that whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be; therefore He said: ﴿does not guide those who mislead﴾, that is, whom He has led astray, so who can guide him after Allah? Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]

Allah, exalted is He, says, reporting about the polytheists: they swore, making the strongest oaths, ﴿by Allah, with their most emphatic oaths﴾, meaning they exerted themselves in swearing and intensified their oaths that ﴿Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾, meaning they considered this far-fetched. So they denied the Messengers in what they told them of this, and swore to its opposite. Allah, exalted is He, said, refuting them and responding to them: ﴿Yes indeed﴾, meaning yes, that will certainly happen, ﴿a promise binding upon Him as truth﴾, meaning there is no escape from it, ﴿but most of mankind do not know﴾, meaning it is out of their ignorance that they oppose the Messengers and fall into disbelief.

Then Allah, exalted is He, mentioned His wisdom in the Return and the raising of bodies on the Day of Mutual Callings, saying: ﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾, meaning to mankind, ﴿that about which they differ﴾, meaning of everything. "When Allah intends a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' in a single word, and it is..."

Meaning: He, exalted is He, needs no emphasis in what He commands, for He cannot be resisted or opposed, because He is the One, the Subduer, the Mighty, whose authority, dominion and majesty have subdued everything. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata' informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: Allah, exalted is He, said: "The son of Adam reviled Me, and it was not fitting for him to revile Me; and he denied Me, and it was not fitting for him to deny Me. Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, informs about His reward for those who emigrate in His cause, seeking His pleasure, who left their homeland, their brothers and their close friends, hoping for Allah's reward and recompense.

It is possible that the occasion of revelation of this noble verse concerns the emigration to Abyssinia, when the harm of their people against them in Makkah became severe, so that they left from among them to the land of Abyssinia, in order to be able to worship their Lord. Among their nobles were Uthman ibn Affan, with him his wife Ruqayyah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, the cousin of the Messenger [[In manuscripts F and A: "the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)".]], and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad [[In manuscripts F and A: "Abd al-Aswad".]], along with a group of nearly eighty, men and women, truthful men and truthful women, may Allah be pleased with them all and make them pleased. Allah did what He did, and He promised them good recompense in this world and the Hereafter, saying: ﴿We will surely settle them in this world in a good place﴾. Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi and Qatadah said: "It is Madinah." It was also said: "Good provision," as Mujahid said.

There is no contradiction between the two opinions, for they left their dwellings and their wealth, so Allah compensated them with something better than them in this world. Whoever leaves something for the sake of Allah, Allah compensates him with what is better for him than it [[In manuscripts T, F and A: "than it in this world".]]. And so it happened: Allah established them in the lands and gave them authority over the necks of the servants, so they became leaders and rulers, and each of them became an imam for the righteous. He also informed that His reward for the emigrants in the Hereafter is greater than what He gave them in this world, saying: ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is greater﴾, meaning greater than what We gave them in this world, ﴿if they only knew﴾, meaning, if those who stayed behind from emigration with them knew what Allah has stored up for those who obey Him and follow His Messenger.

For this reason Hushaym, from al-Awwam, from one who narrated to him, said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, whenever he gave a man from the emigrants his stipend, would say: 'Take it, may Allah bless it for you. This is what Allah promised you in this world, but what He has stored up for you in the Hereafter is better.' Then he recited this verse: ﴿We will surely settle them in this world in a good place, and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/74).]].

Then Allah described them, saying: ﴿Those who are patient and upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning: they were patient over the least harm inflicted on them by their people, relying upon Allah, who made their final outcome good in this world and the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 16, verses 43–44:

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ as a messenger, the Arabs denied that, or some of them did, and they said: "Allah is greater than that His messenger should be a human being." So Allah revealed: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We revealed to a man from among them?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. And He said: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾, meaning: the people of the earlier scriptures. "Were the messengers who came to you humans or angels? If they were angels, you would deny it; and if they were humans, then do not deny that Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger." [And] Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [they were] not from the people of the heaven, as you claimed.

Similarly it was narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, that what is meant by the people of the Reminder is the People of the Book. Mujahid and al-A'mash also said this.

The statement of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, that the Reminder is the Qur'an, citing His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9], is correct, [and] but it is not what is meant here, because the one who denies does not refer, in establishing a matter after denying it, to that very thing.

Likewise the statement of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir: "We are the people of the Reminder," and his meaning that this Ummah is the people of the Reminder, is correct, for this Ummah is more knowledgeable than all the earlier nations, and the scholars of the House of the Messenger, peace and mercy be upon them, are among the best scholars when they follow the straight Sunnah, such as 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, the sons of 'Ali: al-Hasan and al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin, 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir—who is Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn—and Ja'far his son, and their likes, their peers and counterparts, among those who hold fast to the firm rope of Allah and His straight path, who acknowledged to every possessor of a right his right, and placed each in the station that Allah and His Messenger granted him, and to whom the hearts of His believing servants have gathered.

The point is that this noble verse informs that the messengers before Muhammad ﷺ were humans just as he is human, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger? And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ [al-Isra': 93–94], and He the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], and He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal. Then We fulfilled the promise to them and saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors﴾ [al-Anbiya': 8–9], and He said: ﴿Say: I am not something new among the messengers﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I am only a human like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110].

Then Allah the Exalted directed whoever doubted that the messengers were humans to ask the people of the earlier Books about the prophets who had passed: were their prophets humans or angels?

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 16, verses 43–44:

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ as a messenger, the Arabs denied that, or some of them did, and they said: "Allah is greater than that His messenger should be a human being." So Allah revealed: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We revealed to a man from among them?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. And He said: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾, meaning: the people of the earlier scriptures. "Were the messengers who came to you humans or angels? If they were angels, you would deny it; and if they were humans, then do not deny that Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger." [And] Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [they were] not from the people of the heaven, as you claimed.

Similarly it was narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, that what is meant by the people of the Reminder is the People of the Book. Mujahid and al-A'mash also said this.

The statement of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, that the Reminder is the Qur'an, citing His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9], is correct, [and] but it is not what is meant here, because the one who denies does not refer, in establishing a matter after denying it, to that very thing.

Likewise the statement of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir: "We are the people of the Reminder," and his meaning that this Ummah is the people of the Reminder, is correct, for this Ummah is more knowledgeable than all the earlier nations, and the scholars of the House of the Messenger, peace and mercy be upon them, are among the best scholars when they follow the straight Sunnah, such as 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, the sons of 'Ali: al-Hasan and al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin, 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir—who is Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn—and Ja'far his son, and their likes, their peers and counterparts, among those who hold fast to the firm rope of Allah and His straight path, who acknowledged to every possessor of a right his right, and placed each in the station that Allah and His Messenger granted him, and to whom the hearts of His believing servants have gathered.

The point is that this noble verse informs that the messengers before Muhammad ﷺ were humans just as he is human, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger? And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ [al-Isra': 93–94], and He the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], and He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal. Then We fulfilled the promise to them and saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors﴾ [al-Anbiya': 8–9], and He said: ﴿Say: I am not something new among the messengers﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I am only a human like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110].

Ibn Kathir said: He, may He be exalted, tells of His forbearance [and His respite] [[Addition from A.]] and His granting of time to the disobedient who commit evil deeds, call others to them, and deceive people in their calling them to them and driving them toward them. Yet He is able to ﴿cause the earth to swallow them, or let the punishment come upon them from where they do not perceive﴾, meaning: from where they do not know its coming to them. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, so that it shakes [violently]? Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning was﴾ [al-Mulk: 16–17]. His saying ﴿or seize them in their going back and forth﴾ means: in their going back and forth in their livelihoods and their occupation with them, [such as] journeys [in their journeys] [[In A: "with what is in their journeys."]] and similar preoccupying affairs.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿in their going back and forth﴾ means their journeys.

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: ﴿in their going back and forth﴾ means by night and by day, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? * *

Likewise it was narrated from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others.

(2804).]], and in the two Sahihs [[Addition from T, F, A.]]: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." He informs that everything that has a shadow turns its shadow to the right and to the left, that is, in the morning and in the evening, and so it prostrates with its shadow to Allah, exalted is He.

Mujahid said: When the sun passes its zenith, everything prostrates to Allah, mighty and majestic is He. Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others said likewise.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they are humbled (dakhirun)﴾, that is, lowly and abased.

Mujahid also said: The prostration of everything is in it (i.e., the shadow). And when he mentioned the mountains, he said: their prostration is in them.

Abu Ghalib al-Shaybani said: The waves of the sea are its prayer.

He treated them as those who have understanding, since He attributed prostration to them.

Then He said: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures (dabbah)﴾, as He said: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15]. Almighty God tells of the abominable conduct of the polytheists who worshipped other than Allah, the idols, the images, and the rivals, and who assigned to them a share of what Allah had provided for them. They said: ﴿This is for Allah, by their claim, and this is for our partners.' So what is for their partners does not reach Allah [without knowledge] [[addition from "f".]], and what is for Allah reaches their partners.﴾ [Al-An'am: 136]. That is, they assigned to their gods a share alongside Allah, and they also preferred them [[in f: "and preferred it".]] over Him. So Allah swore by His noble Self that He would surely question them about that which they had fabricated and invented, and that He would surely confront them with it and surely recompense them with the fullest recompense in the Fire of Hell. He said: ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾

Then He told of them that they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, into females, and they made them daughters of Allah and worshipped them alongside Him. Thus they erred with a great error in each of these three positions. They attributed to Him a child, though He has no child! Then they gave Him the lesser of the two kinds of offspring, which is daughters, while they themselves would not be pleased with them. As He said: ﴿For you the male, and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division.﴾ [An-Najm: 21, 22]. And here He said: ﴿They assign to Allah daughters, glory be to Him!﴾, that is, above what they say and fabricate. ﴿Surely they are of their own falsehood saying, "Allah has begotten." And indeed they are liars. Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you, how do you judge?﴾ [As-Saffat: 151-154].

* *

His saying: ﴿And for themselves they have what they desire﴾ means: they choose males for themselves and disdain, for themselves, the daughters whom they attributed to Allah. Allah is exalted far above what they say, a great exaltation. For ﴿when one of them is given news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he is full of suppressed grief﴾, that is, sorrowful from distress, ﴿and he is silent﴾, that is, keeping silent from the intensity of what he is in of grief, ﴿he hides himself from the people﴾, that is, he dislikes that people see him, ﴿because of the evil of what he has been given news of. Shall he keep it despite disgrace, or bury it in the dust?﴾ That is, if he keeps her, he keeps her in humiliation, not giving her inheritance, not caring for her, and preferring his male children over her. ﴿Or bury it in the dust﴾, that is, he buries her alive, which is what they used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam). ﴿Is it not evil what they judge?﴾, that is, how evil is what they say, how evil is what they divide, and how evil is what they attribute to Him. As Allah said: ﴿And when one of them is given news of what he has ascribed to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark, and he is full of suppressed grief.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 17]. He, exalted is He, tells of His forbearance toward His creatures despite their wrongdoing, and that if He were to take them to account for what they have earned, He would not leave on the earth's surface a single living creature. That is, He would destroy all the creatures of the earth along with the destruction of the children of Adam. But the Lord, majestic is His majesty, is forbearing and concealing, and He gives respite ﴿until an appointed term﴾. That is, He does not hasten punishment upon them, for if He did so to them He would not leave anyone alive.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, that he said: "The dung beetle (al-ju'al) nearly was punished for the sin of the children of Adam." And he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/85).]].

Similarly, al-A'mash narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, who said: Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud] said: "The dung beetle nearly perished in its hole because of the sin of the children of Adam."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Isma'il ibn Hakim al-Khuza'i narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, who said: Abu Hurayra heard a man saying: "Indeed the wrongdoer harms only himself." He said: So he turned to him and said: "Yes, by Allah, even the bustard dies in its nest from the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/85). Ibn Hajar said: "Its chain includes Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami, who is abandoned (matruk)."]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Musarrih informed us: Sulayman ibn Ata narrated to us, from Maslama ibn Abd Allah, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'a ibn Rib'i, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We mentioned [the matter] in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed Allah does not delay anything when its term has come. The increase in a person's lifespan comes only through a righteous offspring, whom Allah grants to the servant, and they supplicate for him after him, and their supplication reaches him in his grave; that is the increase of his lifespan" [[Also narrated by Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (3/285) through al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik with similar wording, in which Sulayman ibn Ata is agreed to be weak.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾ means: of daughters, and of partners who are [in fact] His servants, while they themselves disdain that any partner of theirs should share in their wealth.

* *

His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best [reward]﴾ is a rebuke against them for their claim, in spite of which they assert that they will have the best [reward] in this world; and even if there is a return, they will have the best [reward] there too. It is also a report of the speech of some of them, like His saying: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing and ungrateful. And if We let him taste favor after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: "The evils have left me." Indeed he is exultant and boastful﴾ [Hud: 9, 10]; and like His saying: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find with Him the best [reward]." So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ [Fussilat: 50]; and His saying: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"? Has he attained the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ [Maryam: 77, 78]; and He related about one of the two men: that he ﴿entered his garden while he was wronging himself, and said, "I do not think this will ever perish, nor do I think the Hour will be established. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find a better return than this"﴾ [al-Kahf: 35, 36]. So these [people] combined evil deeds with the wishful hope of falsehood, [expecting] to be rewarded with good, and this is impossible. As Ibn Ishaq mentioned: a stone was found at the foundation of the Ka'ba when they dismantled it in order to rebuild it, and inscribed upon it were wise sayings and admonitions. Among them: "Do you do evil deeds and are you rewarded with good ones? Indeed, just as grapes are gathered from thorns" [[See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham (1/196).]].

Mujahid and Qatada said: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best [reward]﴾ refers to the boys [i.e., the servants/youths].

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿That for them is the best﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, as we have already explained, and this is the correct view, and to Allah belongs all praise.

For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said, refuting them in their wishful thinking: ﴿Without doubt﴾, that is, truly and inevitably, ﴿that for them is the Fire﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and that they will be neglected﴾ [[Lit. "those who are left behind/abandoned".]].

Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and others said: [it means] "forgotten therein, neglected."

This is like His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs﴾ [al-A'raf: 51]. [[In the text: "ننساكم كما نسيتم" which is an error.]]

Also from Qatada: ﴿Mufrat-un﴾ means "hastened to the Fire," from al-faraṭ, which is one who goes ahead to the watering place. There is no contradiction, for they will be hastened to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and will be forgotten therein, that is, they will abide eternally.

He, exalted is He, tells of His forbearance toward His creatures despite their wrongdoing, and that if He were to take them to account for what they have earned, He would not leave on the earth's surface a single living creature. That is, He would destroy all the creatures of the earth along with the destruction of the children of Adam. But the Lord, majestic is His majesty, is forbearing and concealing, and He gives respite ﴿until an appointed term﴾. That is, He does not hasten punishment upon them, for if He did so to them He would not leave anyone alive.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, that he said: "The dung beetle (al-ju'al) nearly was punished for the sin of the children of Adam." And he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/85).]].

Similarly, al-A'mash narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, who said: Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud] said: "The dung beetle nearly perished in its hole because of the sin of the children of Adam."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Isma'il ibn Hakim al-Khuza'i narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, who said: Abu Hurayra heard a man saying: "Indeed the wrongdoer harms only himself." He said: So he turned to him and said: "Yes, by Allah, even the bustard dies in its nest from the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/85). Ibn Hajar said: "Its chain includes Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami, who is abandoned (matruk)."]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Musarrih informed us: Sulayman ibn Ata narrated to us, from Maslama ibn Abd Allah, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'a ibn Rib'i, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We mentioned [the matter] in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed Allah does not delay anything when its term has come. The increase in a person's lifespan comes only through a righteous offspring, whom Allah grants to the servant, and they supplicate for him after him, and their supplication reaches him in his grave; that is the increase of his lifespan" [[Also narrated by Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (3/285) through al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik with similar wording, in which Sulayman ibn Ata is agreed to be weak.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾ means: of daughters, and of partners who are [in fact] His servants, while they themselves disdain that any partner of theirs should share in their wealth.

* *

His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best [reward]﴾ is a rebuke against them for their claim, in spite of which they assert that they will have the best [reward] in this world; and even if there is a return, they will have the best [reward] there too. It is also a report of the speech of some of them, like His saying: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing and ungrateful. And if We let him taste favor after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: "The evils have left me." Indeed he is exultant and boastful﴾ [Hud: 9, 10]; and like His saying: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find with Him the best [reward]." So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ [Fussilat: 50]; and His saying: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"? Has he attained the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ [Maryam: 77, 78]; and He related about one of the two men: that he ﴿entered his garden while he was wronging himself, and said, "I do not think this will ever perish, nor do I think the Hour will be established. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find a better return than this"﴾ [al-Kahf: 35, 36]. So these [people] combined evil deeds with the wishful hope of falsehood, [expecting] to be rewarded with good, and this is impossible. As Ibn Ishaq mentioned: a stone was found at the foundation of the Ka'ba when they dismantled it in order to rebuild it, and inscribed upon it were wise sayings and admonitions. Among them: "Do you do evil deeds and are you rewarded with good ones? Indeed, just as grapes are gathered from thorns" [[See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham (1/196).]].

Mujahid and Qatada said: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best [reward]﴾ refers to the boys [i.e., the servants/youths].

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿That for them is the best﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, as we have already explained, and this is the correct view, and to Allah belongs all praise.

For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said, refuting them in their wishful thinking: ﴿Without doubt﴾, that is, truly and inevitably, ﴿that for them is the Fire﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and that they will be neglected﴾ [[Lit. "those who are left behind/abandoned".]].

Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and others said: [it means] "forgotten therein, neglected."

This is like His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs﴾ [al-A'raf: 51]. [[In the text: "ننساكم كما نسيتم" which is an error.]]

Also from Qatada: ﴿Mufrat-un﴾ means "hastened to the Fire," from al-faraṭ, which is one who goes ahead to the watering place. There is no contradiction, for they will be hastened to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and will be forgotten therein, that is, they will abide eternally.

Allah, the Exalted, mentions that He sent messengers to the earlier nations, and those messengers were denied. O Muhammad, in your fellow messengers you have an example, so let the denial of your people not grieve you. As for the polytheists who denied the messengers, what led them to that was Satan's adornment of their deeds for them. ﴿So he is their guardian today﴾, meaning: they are under punishment and retribution, Satan is their guardian, he cannot deliver them, and there is no one to help them, and for them there is a painful punishment.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Messenger [in manuscript A: "and said"] that He had only sent down the Book to him [in manuscript A: "sent down"] so that he might make clear to the people that about which they differ. The Qur'an is the decider between people in everything they dispute, ﴿and guidance﴾, meaning for the hearts, ﴿and mercy﴾, meaning for whoever holds fast to it, ﴿for a people who believe﴾.

Just as Allah, the Exalted, made the Qur'an a life for hearts that are dead through disbelief, so [Allah] [addition from manuscript T] revives the earth after its death by the water He sends down on it from the sky. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾, meaning: who understand speech and its meaning.

Allah the Exalted says: "And indeed, for you [O mankind], in the livestock [al-an'am], which are camels, cattle and sheep, is a lesson [a sign and a proof of the power of their Creator, His wisdom, His subtle kindness and His mercy]. We give you drink from what is in their bellies." He used the singular pronoun here, either referring back to the sense of "blessings" (ni'am), or the pronoun refers to the animal, since al-an'am are animals. That is, We give you drink from what is in the belly of this animal.

In another verse: "from what is in their bellies" [Al-Mu'minun: 21]. Both forms are permissible, as in His saying: "Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it" [Al-Muddaththir: 54-55], and in His saying: "And indeed, I am going to send them a gift and see what the messengers return with. So when [the envoy] came to Solomon" [An-Naml: 35-36], meaning: the wealth.

* *

His saying: "From between excrement and blood, pure milk," means that the blood, through its whiteness, its taste and its sweetness, is separated out from between the excrement and the blood inside the animal's body, and each part flows to its place. When the food matures in its stomach, blood is directed into the veins, milk into the udder, urine into the bladder, and dung toward the outlet. Each of these does not mix with the others after it has separated from them, nor is it altered by them.

* *

His saying: "Pure milk, palatable to those who drink it," means that no one chokes on it.

When He mentioned milk, and that He made it a drink for people, palatable, He followed it with mention of what people make from drinks, from the fruits of date palms and grapes, and what they used to produce from intoxicating wine before it was prohibited. For this reason He bestowed favour upon them, saying: "And from the fruits of date palms and grapes you derive intoxicants and good provision." This indicates its permissibility under the Law before its prohibition, and it indicates equality between the intoxicant made from grapes and that made from dates, as is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and the majority of scholars. Likewise is the ruling for all other drinks made from wheat, barley, maize and honey, as the Sunnah has come with detailed explanation of this. This is not the place to expand on it. As Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying, "intoxicant and good provision," he said: "The intoxicant is what is forbidden of their two fruits, and the good provision is what is permitted of their two fruits." In another narration: "Its intoxicant is its unlawful part, and its good provision is its lawful part." That is, what is dried of them, such as dates and raisins, and what is made from them, such as tila' (a drink boiled down from grape juice, and as for dibs, it is date honey and its extract), and vinegar and nabidh (a steeped drink), are lawful to drink before it becomes intoxicating, as the Sunnah has reported.

"Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason." Mention of reason is appropriate here, since it is the noblest faculty in a human being. For this reason Allah prohibited intoxicating drinks to this Ummah, to preserve their minds. Allah the Exalted says: "And We made therein gardens of date palms and grapes, and We caused to gush forth within them springs, that they may eat of their fruit and that which their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful? Exalted is He who created all pairs from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know" [Ya-Sin: 34-36].
