Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verses 68–69:

The meaning of "revelation" (al-wahy) here is inspiration (al-ilham), guidance, and direction given to the bee: to take houses in the mountains, in trees, and in what they erect (﴿and in what they build﴾). Then, the houses are made with the utmost precision in their construction and arrangement, so that there is no flaw among them.

Then God, may He be exalted, gave them permission, a divine decree of subjugation (idhn qadari taskhiri), to eat from all the fruits and to travel the paths that God has made easy for them, meaning easy for them to go wherever they wish in this vast atmosphere, the wide deserts, the valleys, and the towering mountains. Then each one of them returns to its place and its house, not deviating from it to the right or the left, but to its house, where it has its young and its honey. It builds the wax from its wings, vomits the honey from its mouth [[In T: "fam-ha" (its mouth).]], and lays its young from its rear. Then it goes out in the morning to its pastures.

Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿Then follow the ways of your Lord, made easy﴾ means obedient. So they made it a circumstantial clause (hal) of the one who travels. Ibn Zayd said: This is like God's saying, ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72]. He said: Do you not see that they transport the bees [[In T, F, A: "transport with the bees".]] from their hives from one land to another, and it accompanies them?

The first opinion is more apparent, namely that it is a circumstantial clause of the path, meaning: follow it made easy for you. Mujahid explicitly stated this. Ibn Jarir said: Both opinions are correct [[In T, F: "convergent".]].

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili has said: Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Sukayn [[In T, F: "Miskin".]] ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The lifespan of the fly is forty days, and all flies are in the Fire except the bee." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/231), and al-Busiri graded it sound, as in the margin of al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (2/296).]]

* *

God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿There comes out from their bellies a drink, varying in its colors﴾, meaning between white, yellow, red, and other beautiful colors, according to the variety of their pastures and what they eat from them [[In A: "from it".]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Within it is healing for mankind﴾, meaning: in honey there is healing for people from the diseases that afflict them. One of those who spoke on Prophetic medicine (al-tibb al-nabawi, the medicine attributed to the Prophet) said: If He had said "the healing for mankind," it would be a remedy for every disease, but He said ﴿within it is healing for mankind﴾, meaning it is suitable for everyone for cold diseases, since it is hot, and a thing is treated with its opposite.

Mujahid ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr".]] said regarding His saying ﴿within it is healing for mankind﴾: it means the Qur'an.

This is a correct view in itself, but it is not the apparent meaning here from the context of the verse, since the verse only mentions honey, and Mujahid was not followed in his view here. What was said by him is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra': 82], and His saying: ﴿O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ [Yunus: 57].

The proof that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿within it is healing for mankind﴾ is honey is the hadith narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs, through Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil Ali ibn Dawud al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "My brother has an upset stomach." He said: "Give him honey to drink." So he gave him honey to drink, then came back and said: O Messenger of God, I gave him honey to drink, but it only increased his purging! He said: "Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him to drink, then came back and said: O Messenger of God, it only increased his purging! The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied! Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him to drink, and he was cured. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5716) and Sahih Muslim (2217).]]

Some scholars of medicine said: This man had waste matter in him, and when he gave him honey, which is hot, it dissolved it, and it quickly began to be expelled, so his diarrhea increased. The Bedouin thought this harmed him, but it was beneficial for his brother. Then he gave him to drink, and the dissolving and expulsion increased. Then he gave him to drink again, and it was the same. When the corrupt waste harmful to the body had been expelled, his stomach was held firm, his temperament was restored, and the illnesses and pains were removed by the blessing of his [the Prophet's] instruction, upon him be the best of prayers and peace from his Lord. [[See Zad al-Ma'ad by Ibn al-Qayyim (4/33–36) and Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar (10/169, 170).]]

In the two Sahihs, through the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) liked sweets and honey. This is the wording of al-Bukhari. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5682) and Sahih Muslim (1474).]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, through the hadith of Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Healing is in three: in a cupping incision, or a drink of honey, or a cauterization with fire, and I forbid my Ummah from cauterization." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5680, 5681).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "If there is in any of your medicines, or there is in any of your medicines good: then it is in a cupping incision, or a drink of honey, or a sting of fire that suits the disease. And I do not like to be cauterized."

Muslim narrated it through the hadith of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Jabir, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5683) and Sahih Muslim (2205).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abd Allah informed us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed us, Abd Allah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Abu al-Khayr, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three, if there is in anything healing: a cupping incision, or a drink of honey, or a cauterization that causes pain. And I dislike cauterization and do not love it." [[Al-Musnad (4/146).]]

Al-Tabarani narrated it from Harun ibn Mallul [[In H, F: "Mamlul," and in A: "Salul," the form adopted from al-Mu'jam of al-Tabarani.]] al-Misri, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, [from Haywah ibn Shurayh] [[Addition from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani.]] from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, with it. Its wording is: "If there is in anything healing: then a cupping incision..." and he mentioned it... [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/188), al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 9335), and Majma' al-Bahrayn (no. 4165).

Note: In al-Mu'jam al-Awsat it occurs as from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, with it, and he said: "No one narrated it from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid except Sa'id." But I have seen it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, narrated from him by Shurayh, so I do not know whether this is an error or not. And God knows best.]] This is a sound chain, but they did not record it.

Imam Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah al-Qazwini said in his Sunan: Ali ibn Salamah, that is al-Laqqi, narrated to us; Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Upon you are the two cures: honey and the Qur'an." [[Sunan Ibn Majah (3452).]]

This is a good chain. Ibn Majah alone recorded it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet). It was also narrated by Ibn Jarir, from Sufyan ibn Wakee', from his father, from Sufyan, that is al-Thawri, with it, as mawquf (stopping at a companion). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/94). Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal: "The mawquf is more sound."]] And this is more similar.

We have also related from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: If one of you wants a cure, let him write a verse from the Book of God on a dish, and wash it with rainwater, and take a dirham from his wife with her good pleasure, and buy honey with it, and drink it with that, for it is a cure. [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (10/170): "Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it in his Tafsir with a good chain."]] That is, from several aspects. God said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing﴾ [al-Isra': 82], and He said: ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water﴾ [Qaf: 9], and He said: ﴿And if they give you willingly some of it, then eat it, satisfying and wholesome﴾ [al-Nisa': 4], and He said about honey: ﴿Within it is healing for mankind﴾.

Ibn Majah also said: Mahmud ibn Khidash narrated to us; Sa'id ibn Zakariyya al-Qurashi narrated to us; al-Zubayr ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever licks honey three mornings each month, no great calamity will befall him." [[Sunan Ibn Majah (3450). It is also discontinuous: Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim did not hear it from Abu Hurayrah.]]

Al-Zubayr ibn Sa'id is abandoned (matruk) in narration.

Ibn Majah also said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Sarh al-Firyabi narrated to us; Amr ibn Bakr [[In F: "Bakir."]] al-Sakசaki narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Abi Abalah narrated to us. I heard Abu Ibn Umm Haram, who had prayed toward both qiblahs, say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Upon you are al-sanā and al-sanūt, for in them is a cure for every disease except al-sam." It was said: O Messenger of God, what is al-sam? He said: "Death."

Amr said: Ibn Abi Abalah said: "al-sanūt" is dill (shibt). Others said: Rather, it is the honey that [is] [[Addition from T, F, A, and Sunan Ibn Majah.]] in leather skins of ghee, and this is the statement of the poet:

They are ghee with sanut, with no alas (mixing) among them,
and they forbid the neighbor from being humiliated...

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah (3457). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/123): "Its chain is weak," then he gave a defect in it through Amr al-Sakisaki.]] His saying "la alas fihim" means: no mixing. His saying "yamna'una al-jar an yuqarrada" means [they prevent the neighbor from being oppressed and wronged] [[Addition from T, F, A.]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾, meaning: in God's inspiring these weak-created creatures to travel through this wilderness and gather from all kinds of fruits, then collecting them into wax and honey, which is among the best of things, is a sign for a people who give thought about the greatness of their Creator, their Decreer, their Subjector, and their Facilitator. Thereby they infer that He is the Capable (al-Qadir), the Wise (al-Hakim), the Knowing (al-'Alim), the Generous (al-Karim), the Merciful (al-Rahim) [[In the text: "al-Fa'il" (the Doer) was added from F, A.]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verses 68–69:

The meaning of "revelation" (al-wahy) here is inspiration (al-ilham), guidance, and direction given to the bee: to take houses in the mountains, in trees, and in what they erect (﴿and in what they build﴾). Then, the houses are made with the utmost precision in their construction and arrangement, so that there is no flaw among them.

Then God, may He be exalted, gave them permission, a divine decree of subjugation (idhn qadari taskhiri), to eat from all the fruits and to travel the paths that God has made easy for them, meaning easy for them to go wherever they wish in this vast atmosphere, the wide deserts, the valleys, and the towering mountains. Then each one of them returns to its place and its house, not deviating from it to the right or the left, but to its house, where it has its young and its honey. It builds the wax from its wings, vomits the honey from its mouth [[In T: "fam-ha" (its mouth).]], and lays its young from its rear. Then it goes out in the morning to its pastures.

Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿Then follow the ways of your Lord, made easy﴾ means obedient. So they made it a circumstantial clause (hal) of the one who travels. Ibn Zayd said: This is like God's saying, ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72]. He said: Do you not see that they transport the bees [[In T, F, A: "transport with the bees".]] from their hives from one land to another, and it accompanies them?

The first opinion is more apparent, namely that it is a circumstantial clause of the path, meaning: follow it made easy for you. Mujahid explicitly stated this. Ibn Jarir said: Both opinions are correct [[In T, F: "convergent".]].

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili has said: Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Sukayn [[In T, F: "Miskin".]] ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The lifespan of the fly is forty days, and all flies are in the Fire except the bee." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/231), and al-Busiri graded it sound, as in the margin of al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (2/296).]]

* *

God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿There comes out from their bellies a drink, varying in its colors﴾, meaning between white, yellow, red, and other beautiful colors, according to the variety of their pastures and what they eat from them [[In A: "from it".]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Within it is healing for mankind﴾, meaning: in honey there is healing for people from the diseases that afflict them. One of those who spoke on Prophetic medicine (al-tibb al-nabawi, the medicine attributed to the Prophet) said: If He had said "the healing for mankind," it would be a remedy for every disease, but He said ﴿within it is healing for mankind﴾, meaning it is suitable for everyone for cold diseases, since it is hot, and a thing is treated with its opposite.

Mujahid ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr".]] said regarding His saying ﴿within it is healing for mankind﴾: it means the Qur'an.

This is a correct view in itself, but it is not the apparent meaning here from the context of the verse, since the verse only mentions honey, and Mujahid was not followed in his view here. What was said by him is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra': 82], and His saying: ﴿O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ [Yunus: 57].

The proof that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿within it is healing for mankind﴾ is honey is the hadith narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs, through Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil Ali ibn Dawud al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "My brother has an upset stomach." He said: "Give him honey to drink." So he gave him honey to drink, then came back and said: O Messenger of God, I gave him honey to drink, but it only increased his purging! He said: "Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him to drink, then came back and said: O Messenger of God, it only increased his purging! The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied! Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him to drink, and he was cured. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5716) and Sahih Muslim (2217).]]

Some scholars of medicine said: This man had waste matter in him, and when he gave him honey, which is hot, it dissolved it, and it quickly began to be expelled, so his diarrhea increased. The Bedouin thought this harmed him, but it was beneficial for his brother. Then he gave him to drink, and the dissolving and expulsion increased. Then he gave him to drink again, and it was the same. When the corrupt waste harmful to the body had been expelled, his stomach was held firm, his temperament was restored, and the illnesses and pains were removed by the blessing of his [the Prophet's] instruction, upon him be the best of prayers and peace from his Lord. [[See Zad al-Ma'ad by Ibn al-Qayyim (4/33–36) and Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar (10/169, 170).]]

In the two Sahihs, through the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) liked sweets and honey. This is the wording of al-Bukhari. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5682) and Sahih Muslim (1474).]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, through the hadith of Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Healing is in three: in a cupping incision, or a drink of honey, or a cauterization with fire, and I forbid my Ummah from cauterization." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5680, 5681).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "If there is in any of your medicines, or there is in any of your medicines good: then it is in a cupping incision, or a drink of honey, or a sting of fire that suits the disease. And I do not like to be cauterized."

Muslim narrated it through the hadith of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Jabir, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5683) and Sahih Muslim (2205).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abd Allah informed us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed us, Abd Allah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Abu al-Khayr, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three, if there is in anything healing: a cupping incision, or a drink of honey, or a cauterization that causes pain. And I dislike cauterization and do not love it." [[Al-Musnad (4/146).]]

Al-Tabarani narrated it from Harun ibn Mallul [[In H, F: "Mamlul," and in A: "Salul," the form adopted from al-Mu'jam of al-Tabarani.]] al-Misri, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, [from Haywah ibn Shurayh] [[Addition from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani.]] from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, with it. Its wording is: "If there is in anything healing: then a cupping incision..." and he mentioned it... [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/188), al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 9335), and Majma' al-Bahrayn (no. 4165).

Note: In al-Mu'jam al-Awsat it occurs as from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, with it, and he said: "No one narrated it from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid except Sa'id." But I have seen it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, narrated from him by Shurayh, so I do not know whether this is an error or not. And God knows best.]] This is a sound chain, but they did not record it.

Imam Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah al-Qazwini said in his Sunan: Ali ibn Salamah, that is al-Laqqi, narrated to us; Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Upon you are the two cures: honey and the Qur'an." [[Sunan Ibn Majah (3452).]]

This is a good chain. Ibn Majah alone recorded it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet). It was also narrated by Ibn Jarir, from Sufyan ibn Wakee', from his father, from Sufyan, that is al-Thawri, with it, as mawquf (stopping at a companion). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/94). Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal: "The mawquf is more sound."]] And this is more similar.

We have also related from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: If one of you wants a cure, let him write a verse from the Book of God on a dish, and wash it with rainwater, and take a dirham from his wife with her good pleasure, and buy honey with it, and drink it with that, for it is a cure. [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (10/170): "Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it in his Tafsir with a good chain."]] That is, from several aspects. God said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing﴾ [al-Isra': 82], and He said: ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water﴾ [Qaf: 9], and He said: ﴿And if they give you willingly some of it, then eat it, satisfying and wholesome﴾ [al-Nisa': 4], and He said about honey: ﴿Within it is healing for mankind﴾.

Ibn Majah also said: Mahmud ibn Khidash narrated to us; Sa'id ibn Zakariyya al-Qurashi narrated to us; al-Zubayr ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever licks honey three mornings each month, no great calamity will befall him." [[Sunan Ibn Majah (3450). It is also discontinuous: Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim did not hear it from Abu Hurayrah.]]

Al-Zubayr ibn Sa'id is abandoned (matruk) in narration.

Ibn Majah also said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Sarh al-Firyabi narrated to us; Amr ibn Bakr [[In F: "Bakir."]] al-Sakசaki narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Abi Abalah narrated to us. I heard Abu Ibn Umm Haram, who had prayed toward both qiblahs, say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Upon you are al-sanā and al-sanūt, for in them is a cure for every disease except al-sam." It was said: O Messenger of God, what is al-sam? He said: "Death."

Amr said: Ibn Abi Abalah said: "al-sanūt" is dill (shibt). Others said: Rather, it is the honey that [is] [[Addition from T, F, A, and Sunan Ibn Majah.]] in leather skins of ghee, and this is the statement of the poet:

They are ghee with sanut, with no alas (mixing) among them,
and they forbid the neighbor from being humiliated...

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah (3457). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/123): "Its chain is weak," then he gave a defect in it through Amr al-Sakisaki.]] His saying "la alas fihim" means: no mixing. His saying "yamna'una al-jar an yuqarrada" means [they prevent the neighbor from being oppressed and wronged] [[Addition from T, F, A.]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾, meaning: in God's inspiring these weak-created creatures to travel through this wilderness and gather from all kinds of fruits, then collecting them into wax and honey, which is among the best of things, is a sign for a people who give thought about the greatness of their Creator, their Decreer, their Subjector, and their Facilitator. Thereby they infer that He is the Capable (al-Qadir), the Wise (al-Hakim), the Knowing (al-'Alim), the Generous (al-Karim), the Merciful (al-Rahim) [[In the text: "al-Fa'il" (the Doer) was added from F, A.]].

Allah, Exalted is He, informs us about His disposal of His servants: it is He who brought them into existence from non-existence, then after that causes them to die. Among them is one whom He leaves until old age reaches him (al-haram), which is weakness in one's creation,

as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.﴾ [al-Rum: 54].

It has been narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding the most degraded age (ardhal al-'umr), that it is seventy-five years. At this age there occurs for him weakness of faculties, senility (al-kharaf), poor memory, and little knowledge. For this reason He said: ﴿so that he knows nothing after having known﴾, meaning: after he had been knowledgeable, he becomes one who knows nothing of anything, due to senility (al-fanad) and dotage (al-kharaf). For this reason al-Bukhari narrated, when commenting on this verse:

Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Harun ibn Musa Abu 'Abd Allah al-A'war narrated to us, from Shu'ayb, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate: "I seek refuge in You from miserliness and laziness, and from senility (al-haram) and the most degraded age, and from the punishment of the grave, and from the trial of the Dajjal, and from the trials of life and death."

Muslim also narrated it, from the hadith of Harun al-A'war, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4707) and Sahih Muslim no. (2706); "al-haram" is not in the Sahih].

Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said in his famous Mu'allaqa:

I have grown weary of the burdens of life, and whoever lives eighty years, by your father, becomes weary.

I have seen death as a blind she-camel: whoever it strikes, it destroys him, and whoever it misses, lives long and grows senile.

[Diwan of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (p. 29).]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 16, verse 71:

يُبَيِّنُ تَعَالَى لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ جَهْلَهُمْ وَكُفْرَهُمْ فِيمَا زَعَمُوهُ [[في ت، ف: "يزعمون".]] لِلَّهِ مِنَ الشُّرَكَاءِ، وَهُمْ يَعْتَرِفُونَ [[في ت، ف، أ: "يعرفون".]] أَنَّهَا عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، كَمَا كَانُوا يَقُولُونَ فِي تَلْبِيَاتِهِمْ فِي حَجِّهِمْ: "لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، إِلَّا شَرِيكًا هُوَ لَكَ، تَمْلِكُهُ وَمَا مَلَكَ".

God, Exalted is He, makes clear to the polytheists their ignorance and disbelief regarding the partners they attribute to Him [[In t, f: "they attribute" (present tense).]], while they acknowledge that these are His servants (talbiyah), as they used to say in their pilgrimage call (talbiyah): "Here I am, O Allah, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You possess him and all that he possesses." Then God, Exalted is He, rebukes them, saying: "You yourselves would not be content to be equal with your slaves in what We have provided for you. How then would He be content for His servants to be equal to Him in divinity and exaltation?" As He says in another verse: ﴿He has coined for you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein and fear them as you fear one another?﴾ [Ar-Rum: 28].

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: He says: "They would not make their slaves partners with them in their wealth and their women, so how do they make My servants partners with Me in My dominion?" This is His saying: ﴿Then is it the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾

In another narration from him: "How do you find acceptable for Me what you do not find acceptable for yourselves?"

Mujahid said regarding this verse: "This is the likeness of the false gods."

Qatadah said: "This is an example which Allah has set forth: Is there anyone among you who would share his slave in his wife and his bed, so that you would make the creatures and servants of Allah equal to Him? If you would not accept this for yourself, then Allah is more worthy to be exalted above you."

* *

His saying: ﴿Then is it the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾ means: they assigned to Allah a portion of what He created of tilth and livestock, and so they denied His blessing and associated others with Him.

From al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote this letter to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: "Be content with your provision from this world, for the Most Merciful has preferred some of His servants over others in provision, but He tests each by it, and He tests the one whose provision He extends: how does he give thanks to Allah, and how does he fulfil the right which He has made obligatory upon him in what He has provided and bestowed upon him?" Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verse 72:

He, may He be exalted, mentions His blessings upon His servants: that He made for them spouses from among themselves, of their own kind and form [and their adornment]. Had He made the spouses of another species, there would not have come about affection (ii'tilaf), love (mawaddah) and mercy (rahmah). Rather, out of His mercy, He created from the children of Adam males and females, and made the females spouses for the males.

Then He, may He be exalted, mentioned that He made from the spouses "sons (banin) and grandchildren (hafadah)", and the hafadah are the children of the sons. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd.

Shu'bah said, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Banin and hafadah" are the child and the child's child.

Sunayd said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Your sons, when they serve you (yahfidunaka), assist you (yarfidunaka), help you (yu'inunaka) and serve you (yakhdimunaka)." Jamil said:

"The servant-girls served around them, and they gave over
into their hands the reins of the camels."

Mujahid said: "Banin and hafadah" are his son and his servant. And in another narration he said: the hafadah are the helpers (al-ansar), the aides (al-a'wan) and the servants (al-khuddam).

Tawus said: the hafadah are the servants (al-khadam), and likewise said Qatadah, Abu Malik and al-Hasan al-Basri.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah that he said: the hafadah are whoever among your children and your children's children serves you.

al-Dahhak said: The Arabs used to be served by their sons.

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words: "And He made for you from your spouses sons and hafadah," he says: the sons of a man's wife who are not his own. It is also said: the hafadah are the man who works before a man; it is said, "So-and-so serves (yahfidu) for us." He said: And some men claim that the hafadah are the brothers-in-law (akhtan) of the man.

This last opinion, which Ibn 'Abbas mentioned, was also said by Ibn Mas'ud, Masruq, Abu al-Duha, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and al-Qurazi. 'Ikrimah narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the in-laws (al-asharr).

Ibn Jarir said: All these opinions fall within the meaning of "al-hafd," which is service (al-khidmah), from which comes His words in the qunut: "And to You we strive and serve (nahfid)." And since service may come from children, in-laws and servants, the blessing is achieved through all of this; therefore He said: "And He made for you from your spouses sons and hafadah."

I say: Whoever makes "hafadah" dependent on "azwajikum" must mean the children, the children's children, and the in-laws, because they are the husbands of the daughters and the children of the wife; and as al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak said, they are generally under a man's care, in his custody and in his service. This may be what is meant by the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the hadith of Basrah ibn Akthan: "And the child is a slave to you." Abu Dawud narrated it.

As for the one who makes the hafadah the servants, in his view it is coordinated (ma'tuf) with His words: "And Allah made for you spouses from your own selves," meaning: and He made for you spouses and children.

"And He provided for you from the good things (al-tayyibat)," of foods and drinks.

Then He, may He be exalted, said, rebuking those who associate others in worshipping the Benefactor: "Then in falsehood do they believe?" and they are the idols and rivals; "and in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?" meaning: they conceal the blessings of Allah upon them and attribute them to others.

And in the authentic hadith: "Allah, may He be exalted, will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection, reminding him of favours: 'Did I not marry you? Did I not honour you? Did I not subject to you horses and camels, and leave you to lead and to pasture?'" Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Allah says, reporting about the polytheists who worshipped others alongside Him, although He alone is the Bestower of blessings, the Bountiful, the Creator, the Provider, with no partner, and despite this they worship besides Him idols, rivals and images, ﴿that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth, [any] at all﴾. That is: it cannot send down rain, nor cause grain or trees to grow, and they do not possess that, meaning that it does not belong to them, and they are not able to do it even if they wished to. For this reason Allah says, ﴿So do not strike forth examples for Allah﴾, meaning: do not make for Him rivals, likenesses and equals. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, meaning: He knows and bears witness that there is no deity except Allah, while you, out of your ignorance, associate others with Him.

Allah says, reporting about the polytheists who worshipped others alongside Him, although He alone is the Bestower of blessings, the Bountiful, the Creator, the Provider, with no partner, and despite this they worship besides Him idols, rivals and images, ﴿that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth, [any] at all﴾. That is: it cannot send down rain, nor cause grain or trees to grow, and they do not possess that, meaning that it does not belong to them, and they are not able to do it even if they wished to. For this reason Allah says, ﴿So do not strike forth examples for Allah﴾, meaning: do not make for Him rivals, likenesses and equals. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, meaning: He knows and bears witness that there is no deity except Allah, while you, out of your ignorance, associate others with Him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verse 75:

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "This is a parable that Allah struck for the disbeliever and the believer." Qatadah said likewise, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view.

The slave [[In T and F: "So the slave."]] who has no power over anything is like the disbeliever, and the one who is given good provision, so he spends from it secretly and openly, is the believer.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "It is a parable struck for the idol (wathan) and for the Truth, Most High. Can these two be equal?"

Since the difference between them is clear, evident and manifest, and none ignores it except every fool, Allah Most High said: ﴿Praise be to Allah; but most of them do not know.﴾ [Then Allah Most High said] [[Added from T, F and A.]]

Mujahid said: "This also refers to the idol and to the Exalted One, meaning: the idol is mute, unable to speak or utter anything good or anything at all [[In manuscripts T and A: "or a human being."]], and it has no power over anything whatsoever, neither speech nor action. Yet despite this, it is ﴿a burden﴾, that is, a dependent and a encumbrance upon its master. ﴿Wherever he sends him﴾, that is, dispatches him, ﴿he brings no good﴾ and his errand does not succeed. ﴿Are they equal?﴾ meaning, are those who have these attributes equal to ﴿one who enjoins justice﴾, that is, equity, whose speech is true and whose actions are upright, ﴿and he is on a straight path﴾." This was also the view of al-Suddi, Qatadah and Ata al-Khurasani, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) preferred this opinion.

Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas that it is also an example for the disbeliever and the believer, as mentioned earlier.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sailhini narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Ikrimah, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿God sets forth an example: a slave owned, who has no power over anything﴾ — it was revealed concerning a man of Quraysh and his slave. And regarding His words: ﴿God sets forth an example: two men, one of them mute, who has no power over anything﴾ up to His words: ﴿and he is on a straight path﴾, he said: "He is Uthman ibn Affan." He said: "And the mute one, wherever he sends him he brings no good," he said: "He is a client (mawla) of Uthman ibn Affan. Uthman used to spend on him, support him, and provide for his needs, while the other one hated Islam, rejected it, and forbade (people) from charity and good deeds. So these verses were revealed concerning the two of them." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/101).]]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs of His perfection and His power over things. In His knowledge is the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and He alone is singled out with it, so no one has access to it except that Allah, exalted is He, informs whomever He wills of it. As He said: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50], meaning that what He wills comes into being as quickly as the blink of an eye. Likewise He said here: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye, or it is nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things Competent﴾, just as He said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but like that of a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28].

Then He mentioned His favour upon His servants in bringing them out from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing. Then after this Allah, exalted is He, grants them hearing, by which they perceive sounds, and sight, by which they sense visible things, and hearts (af'idah), which are the intellects, whose seat is the heart according to the correct view; it was also said that it is the brain. By intellect one distinguishes between things, harmful and beneficial. These powers and senses are acquired by a human gradually, little by little; as he grows, his hearing, sight and intellect increase until he reaches his maturity (ashuddah).

His saying ﴿And Allah has made for you, of what He created, shades﴾. Qatadah said: it means trees.

﴿And He has made for you of the mountains refuges﴾, that is, fortresses and places of refuge. And ﴿He has made for you garments to protect you from the heat﴾, and these are garments of cotton, linen, and wool. ﴿And garments to protect you from your violence﴾, like coats of mail of hammered iron, and chain mail, and other such things. ﴿Thus He completes His blessing upon you﴾, that is, in this way He makes for you what you use to aid you in your affairs and what you need, so that it may be an aid to you in His obedience and worship. ﴿So that you may submit (tuslimun)﴾.

This is how the majority of scholars (al-jumhur) explained it, and they recited "tuslimun" with a kasra on the lam, meaning from Islam (al-Islam).

Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Thus He completes His blessing upon you [so that you may submit]﴾, said: this surah is called the Surah of Blessings.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated from Hanzalah al-Sadusi, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it "taslamun" with a fatha on the lam, meaning from wounds. Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated it from Abbad, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) recorded it through both channels, but he rejected this recitation. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/104).]

Ata' al-Khurasani said: the Qur'an was revealed according to the measure of the Arabs' understanding. Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has made for you, of what He created, shades, and has made for you of the mountains refuges﴾? What He made for them of plains is greater and more abundant, but they were people of mountains. Do you not see His saying: ﴿and from their wool, their fur, and their hair, goods and provision for a time﴾?

What He made for them of other than that is greater and more abundant than it, but they were people of fur and hair. Do you not see His saying: ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail in them﴾ [al-Nur: 43], because of their wonder at it, while what He sends down of snow is greater and more abundant, but they did not know it? Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿garments to protect you from the heat﴾, while what remains of cold is greater and more abundant, but they were people of heat.

* *

His saying ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, after this clarification and this favour, ﴿then upon you is only the clear conveyance﴾, and you have conveyed it to them.

﴿They recognize the blessing of Allah, then they deny it﴾, that is, they know that Allah, Exalted is He, is the One who bestows this upon them and grants it to them as a bounty, yet despite this they deny it, worship others besides Him, and attribute victory and provision to others. ﴿And most of them are disbelievers.﴾ As Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Safwan related to us, al-Walid related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir related to us, from Mujahid, that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to him: ﴿And Allah has made for you from your houses a dwelling﴾. The Bedouin said: Yes. He said: ﴿And He has made for you from the hides of cattle houses, which you find light on the day of your travel and the day of your stay﴾. The Bedouin said: Yes. He recited to him all of it, and each time the Bedouin said: Yes, until he reached: ﴿Thus He completes His blessing upon you, so that you may submit﴾. Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 16, verses 84–88:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about the condition of the polytheists on the Day of their return to Him in the Hereafter, and that He will raise up from every nation a witness, who is its prophet, testifying against it concerning how it responded to what he conveyed to it from Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Then the disbelievers will not be permitted [to offer excuses]﴾, meaning they will not be permitted to make excuses, because they know that their excuses are false and untrue, as He said: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be given permission so that they may make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35–36]. For this reason He said: ﴿Nor will they be allowed to seek to make amends. And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them﴾, meaning those who committed shirk, ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, meaning it will not be delayed for them. Rather, they will be seized swiftly from the place of standing without any reckoning. When Hell is brought forth, it will be led by seventy thousand bridles, with seventy thousand angels holding each bridle, and a neck of it will extend over the creatures. It will emit a roar such that no one remains except that he falls to his knees. It will say: "I have been entrusted with every tyrant and obstinate one, who set up another god with Allah, and with such-and-such," and it will mention categories of people, as has come in the hadith. Then it will gather them in and pick them up from the place of standing as a bird picks up grain. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring. And when they are cast into a narrow place therein, bound together, they will call out there for destruction. Do not call out for one destruction today, but call out for many destructions﴾ [al-Furqan: 12–14]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The criminals will see the Fire and will think that they are about to fall into it, and they will find no escape from it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped. Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Anbiya: 39–40].

Then Allah, the Exalted, informed us of the disavowal of their deities of them at the time they most need them. He said: ﴿When those who committed shirk see their partners﴾, meaning those whom they used to worship in the world, ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You." But they will throw back at them the word: "Indeed, you are liars"﴾, meaning the deities will say to them: "You are lying; we did not command you to worship us." As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 5–6]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They have taken gods besides Allah in order that they may be a source of honour for them. No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾ [Maryam: 81–82]. And al-Khalil (Abraham), upon him be peace, said: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 25]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the Day when He will say: "Call upon My partners whom you claimed," they will call upon them but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ [al-Kahf: 52]. The verses on this subject are numerous.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will submit to Allah on that Day﴾, Qatadah and Ikrimah said: they will be humbled and will submit on that Day, meaning they will all submit to Allah, so none will be anything but one who hears and obeys, as He said: ﴿How well they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us!﴾ [Maryam: 38], meaning how acute their hearing and sight will be that Day! And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If only you could see the criminals hanging their heads before their Lord, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back and we will do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12]. And He said: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾ [Ta-Ha: 111], meaning they will be humbled, abased, subdued, returning in repentance and submitting.

﴿And they will submit to Allah on that Day, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾, meaning that what they used to worship, falsely attributing it to Allah, will be gone and will perish, so they will have no helper, no assistant, and no one to grant them protection.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the path of Allah – We will increase their punishment upon punishment because of the corruption they used to cause﴾, meaning a punishment for their disbelief and a punishment for their barring people from following the truth. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾ [al-An'am: 26], meaning they forbid people from following it and they themselves also keep far from it. ﴿And they destroy none but themselves, though they are not aware﴾ [al-An'am: 26]. This is evidence of the variation among the disbelievers in their punishment, just as the believers vary in their stations in Paradise and their ranks, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿He will say: "For each there is double, but you do not know"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith) Abu Ya'la said: Shuraih ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah, concerning Allah's saying: ﴿We will increase their punishment upon punishment﴾. He said: "Scorpions will be added whose fangs are like tall palm trees."¹

And Shuraih ibn Yunus narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Ibn Abbas that he said concerning ﴿We will increase their punishment upon punishment﴾: "They are five rivers beneath the Throne, by some of which they will be punished at night and by some of which they will be punished by day."²

¹ [Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/66); and al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (14/107) via Abu Mu'awiyah from al-A'mash with the same chain.]

² [Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/66). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/390): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

﴿And they will submit to Allah on that Day, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾, meaning that what they used to worship, falsely attributing it to Allah, will be gone and will perish, so they will have no helper, no assistant, and no one to grant them protection.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the path of Allah – We will increase their punishment upon punishment because of the corruption they used to cause﴾, meaning a punishment for their disbelief and a punishment for their barring people from following the truth. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾ [al-An'am: 26], meaning they forbid people from following it and they themselves also keep far from it. ﴿And they destroy none but themselves, though they are not aware﴾ [al-An'am: 26]. This is evidence of the variation among the disbelievers in their punishment, just as the believers vary in their stations in Paradise and their ranks, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿He will say: "For each there is double, but you do not know"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith) Abu Ya'la said: Shuraih ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah, concerning Allah's saying: ﴿We will increase their punishment upon punishment﴾. He said: "Scorpions will be added whose fangs are like tall palm trees."¹

And Shuraih ibn Yunus narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Ibn Abbas that he said concerning ﴿We will increase their punishment upon punishment﴾: "They are five rivers beneath the Throne, by some of which they will be punished at night and by some of which they will be punished by day."²

¹ [Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/66); and al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (14/107) via Abu Mu'awiyah from al-A'mash with the same chain.]

² [Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/66). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/390): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 16, verses 84–88:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about the condition of the polytheists on the Day of their return to Him in the Hereafter, and that He will raise up from every nation a witness, who is its prophet, testifying against it concerning how it responded to what he conveyed to it from Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Then the disbelievers will not be permitted [to offer excuses]﴾, meaning they will not be permitted to make excuses, because they know that their excuses are false and untrue, as He said: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be given permission so that they may make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35–36]. For this reason He said: ﴿Nor will they be allowed to seek to make amends. And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them﴾, meaning those who committed shirk, ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, meaning it will not be delayed for them. Rather, they will be seized swiftly from the place of standing without any reckoning. When Hell is brought forth, it will be led by seventy thousand bridles, with seventy thousand angels holding each bridle, and a neck of it will extend over the creatures. It will emit a roar such that no one remains except that he falls to his knees. It will say: "I have been entrusted with every tyrant and obstinate one, who set up another god with Allah, and with such-and-such," and it will mention categories of people, as has come in the hadith. Then it will gather them in and pick them up from the place of standing as a bird picks up grain. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring. And when they are cast into a narrow place therein, bound together, they will call out there for destruction. Do not call out for one destruction today, but call out for many destructions﴾ [al-Furqan: 12–14]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The criminals will see the Fire and will think that they are about to fall into it, and they will find no escape from it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped. Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Anbiya: 39–40].

Then Allah, the Exalted, informed us of the disavowal of their deities of them at the time they most need them. He said: ﴿When those who committed shirk see their partners﴾, meaning those whom they used to worship in the world, ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You." But they will throw back at them the word: "Indeed, you are liars"﴾, meaning the deities will say to them: "You are lying; we did not command you to worship us." As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 5–6]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They have taken gods besides Allah in order that they may be a source of honour for them. No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾ [Maryam: 81–82]. And al-Khalil (Abraham), upon him be peace, said: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 25]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the Day when He will say: "Call upon My partners whom you claimed," they will call upon them but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ [al-Kahf: 52]. The verses on this subject are numerous.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will submit to Allah on that Day﴾, Qatadah and Ikrimah said: they will be humbled and will submit on that Day, meaning they will all submit to Allah, so none will be anything but one who hears and obeys, as He said: ﴿How well they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us!﴾ [Maryam: 38], meaning how acute their hearing and sight will be that Day! And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If only you could see the criminals hanging their heads before their Lord, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back and we will do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12]. And He said: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾ [Ta-Ha: 111], meaning they will be humbled, abased, subdued, returning in repentance and submitting.

﴿And they will submit to Allah on that Day, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾, meaning that what they used to worship, falsely attributing it to Allah, will be gone and will perish, so they will have no helper, no assistant, and no one to grant them protection.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the path of Allah – We will increase their punishment upon punishment because of the corruption they used to cause﴾, meaning a punishment for their disbelief and a punishment for their barring people from following the truth. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾ [al-An'am: 26], meaning they forbid people from following it and they themselves also keep far from it. ﴿And they destroy none but themselves, though they are not aware﴾ [al-An'am: 26]. This is evidence of the variation among the disbelievers in their punishment, just as the believers vary in their stations in Paradise and their ranks, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿He will say: "For each there is double, but you do not know"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

He said: "Scorpions will be added whose fangs are like tall palm trees."¹
