Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 16, verse 89:

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And [remember] the Day when We will raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We will bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these.﴾ [[In manuscript T: "yabʿathu" (singular).]] That is, against his ummah.

Meaning: remember that Day and its terror, and what Allah has granted you in it of great honour and exalted station. This verse is similar to the verse at which ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud stopped when he recited the beginning of Surah an-Nisa to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he reached the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿How, then, [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [an-Nisa: 41], the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "That is enough for you." Ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "So I turned, and his eyes were shedding tears." [[The hadith's takhrij was mentioned previously at the commentary on verse 41 of Surah an-Nisa.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾, Ibn Masʿud said: [And] [[addition from manuscript F.]] "He has explained to us in this Qur'an every knowledge and every thing."

Mujahid said: "Every lawful and unlawful matter."

The saying of Ibn Masʿud is more general and comprehensive, for the Qur'an includes every beneficial knowledge: the report of what came before, the knowledge of what is yet to come, the ruling on every lawful and unlawful matter, and everything people need in the affairs of their worldly life and religion, their livelihood and their return (to Allah).

﴿And guidance﴾, that is, for the hearts, ﴿and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.﴾

Al-Awza'i said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾, that is, through the Sunnah.

The connection between His saying ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book﴾ and His saying ﴿and We bring you as a witness against these﴾ is that the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: The One who obligated you to convey the Book He sent down to you will question you about that on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6]; ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92–93]; ﴿The Day Allah will assemble the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return﴾ [al-Qasas: 85], that is: Indeed, He who made it obligatory upon you to convey the Qur'an will surely return you to Himself, restore you on the Day of Resurrection, and question you about your discharge of what was imposed upon you. This is one of the opinions, and it is a sound and good one.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 16, verse 90:

He, exalted is He, informs that He commands His servants to be just (al-'adl), which is equity and balance, and urges them to excellence (al-ihsan), as He said: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ [An-Nahl: 126], and He said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura: 40], and He said: ﴿And the wounds are subject to retaliation. But whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 45], along with other verses indicating this, concerning the legislation of justice and the urging towards virtue.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾ that he said: It is the testimony that there is no deity except Allah.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: Justice in this context is: the equality of the inner and outer state of every person who does a deed for Allah. And excellence (ihsan) is: that his inner state is better than his outer state. And indecency (al-fahsha') and the reprehensible (al-munkar) are: that his outer state is better than his inner state.

* *

His saying ﴿and giving to the near of kin﴾ means: He commands the maintenance of ties of kinship, as He said: ﴿And give the near of kin his right, and the needy and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully﴾ [Al-Isra': 26].

* *

His saying ﴿And He forbids immorality and bad conduct﴾: al-fawahish (immoral acts) are the prohibited things, and al-munkarat (bad conduct) are what is apparent of them from their doer. This is why it was said in another place: ﴿Say, "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 33]. As for al-baghy (oppression), it is transgression against people. There has come in a hadith: "There is no sin more deserving that Allah hastens its punishment in this world, along with what is stored up for its doer in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing of the ties of kinship" [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (5/36), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan (no. 4902), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan (no. 2511), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan (no. 4211), from the hadith of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."].

* *

His saying ﴿He admonishes you﴾ means: He commands you with what He commands of good, and forbids you from what He forbids of evil, ﴿so that you may remember﴾.

Al-Sha'bi related from Shutayr ibn Shakal: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: The most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an in Surah An-Nahl is: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾, the verse. Narrated by Ibn Jarir [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/109)].

Sa'id related from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾, the verse: There is no good character that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to practice and regard as good except that Allah commanded it, and there is no bad character that they used to reproach one another for except that Allah forbade it and warned against it. He only forbade the base and reprehensible characters.

I (Ibn Kathir) say: This is why there has come in a hadith: "Indeed, Allah loves the noble characters and dislikes the base ones" [Narrated by al-Kharaʾiti in Makarim al-Akhlaq (no. 3), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (8/255), via Ma'mar, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, raised to the Prophet. Abu Nu'aym said: "It is gharib from the hadith of Abu Hazim and Sahl; Ma'mar alone narrated it from Abu Hazim."].

Al-Hafiz Abu Nu'aym said in his book "Kitab Ma'rifat al-Sahabah": Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Fath al-Hanbali narrated to us, Yahya ibn Muhammad, mawla of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Munkadiri narrated to us, 'Umar ibn 'Ali al-Muqaddami narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr [in some manuscripts: "'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayr," which is an error; see Ma'rifat al-Sahabah (2/420), al-Thiqat of Ibn Hibban (7/207), and al-Isabah (1/118)], from his father, who said: The news of the emergence of the Prophet ﷺ reached Aktham ibn Sayfi, and he wanted to go to him, but his people refused to let him and said: "You are our elder; you must not hasten to him!" He said: "Then let someone go to him who will convey my message to him and convey his message to me." Two men volunteered and came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "We are the messengers of Aktham ibn Sayfi, and he asks you: Who are you? And what are you?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "As for who I am, I am Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah. And as for what I am, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger." He said: Then he recited to them this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence and giving to the near of kin, and forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that you may remember﴾. They said: "Repeat this statement to us," and he repeated it to them until they memorized it. Then they came to Aktham and said: "He refused to state his lineage, so we asked about his lineage and found him to be of pure lineage, central among Mudar, and he has thrown to us words we have heard." When Aktham heard them he said: "I think he commands noble characters and forbids their opposites. So be leaders in this matter, and do not be followers in it" [Ma'rifat al-Sahabah (2/420). Ibn Hajar said: "It is mursal." Ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned it in al-Isti'ab (1/146) and denied that Aktham ibn Sayfi was a Companion. See al-Isabah (1/119)].

A good hadith has also been transmitted concerning the revelation of this noble verse, narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, saying: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the courtyard of his house, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un passed by him, and he made a gesture to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Will you not sit?" He said: "Yes." He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat facing him, and while he was conversing with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fixed his gaze toward the sky, looked for a while at the sky, then began lowering his gaze until he placed it on his right side on the ground. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned from his companion 'Uthman toward where he had placed his gaze, and began nodding his head as if he were understanding what was being said to him, while Ibn Maz'un was watching. When he had finished his need and understood what was said to him, the gaze of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose toward the sky as it had the first time. He followed it with his gaze until it disappeared into the sky. Then he turned to 'Uthman in his first sitting position and said: "O Muhammad, what was I sitting with you for? I have never seen you do what you did this morning!" He said: "And what did you see me do?" He said: "I saw your gaze fixed on the sky, then you placed it where you placed it on your right, and you turned toward it and left me, and you began nodding your head as if you were understanding something said to you." He said: "And did you notice that?" 'Uthman said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Messenger of Allah came to me just now while you were sitting." He said: "The Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What did he say to you?" He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence and giving to the near of kin, and forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that you may remember﴾. 'Uthman said: "That was when faith settled in my heart, and I loved Muhammad ﷺ" [Al-Musnad (1/318)].

An isnad that is good, connected, and hasan; the connected hearing has been made clear in it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, in abridged form.

Another hadith: from 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As al-Thaqafi concerning this. Imam Ahmad said:

Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Huraym narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when his gaze became fixed, and he said: "Jibril came to me and commanded me to place this verse in this position of this surah: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence [and giving to the near of kin, and forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that you may remember]﴾" [Al-Musnad (4/218)].

This isnad is acceptable (la ba'sa bihi), and perhaps it is through Shahr ibn Hawshab in both ways, and Allah knows best.

This is commanded by God Most High: fulfilling covenants and pledges, and maintaining firm oaths. Hence He said: ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾.

There is no contradiction between this and His words: ﴿And do not make Allah the target of your oaths [to be] righteous and mindful of Allah and to make peace between people﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 224], and His words: ﴿That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. And guard your oaths﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 89], meaning: do not leave them without expiation; and His words, peace be upon him, in what is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "By Allah, if Allah wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I do what is better and make expiation for my oath." And in another narration: "and I expiate for my oath." There is no contradiction among all of these, nor between them and the aforementioned verse, ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation, and you have made Allah your surety﴾, because these oaths meant are those included in covenants and pledges, not the oaths that are given to urge or to prevent. Hence Mujahid said regarding His words ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾: it means the alliance, i.e., the alliances of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period). This is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abdullah ibn Muhammad, that is Ibn Abi Shaybah, related to us: Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah related to us, from Zakariyya, that is Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance existed in the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased it in firmness."

Muslim also narrated it similarly from Ibn Abi Shaybah.

Its meaning is that in Islam there is no need for the alliance that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to make, for adherence to Islam is sufficient in place of what they were in.

As for what is reported in the Two Sahihs, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made an alliance between the Muhajirun and the Ansar in our house" — its meaning is that he established brotherhood between them, so they would inherit from one another by it, until Allah abrogated that. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi related to me, Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, Ibn Abi Layla informed us, from Muzayyidah [in another copy: Buraydah], concerning His words ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have covenanted﴾, he said: it was revealed concerning the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ). Whoever embraced Islam pledged allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ) upon Islam, so He said: ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have covenanted﴾ — this is the pledge you pledged upon Islam; ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ — the pledge. Let not the fewness of Muhammad [and his companions] and the multitude of the polytheists lead you to break the pledge you made upon Islam.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il related to us, Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi', who said: When the people deposed Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, Ibn Umar gathered his sons and family, then he recited the tashahhud, then said: "To proceed: we have pledged allegiance to this man upon the pledge of Allah and His Messenger, and I have heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, the treacherous one will have a banner raised for him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so. And among the greatest treachery—except associating partners with Allah—is that a man pledges allegiance to a man upon the pledge of Allah and His Messenger, then breaks his pledge. So let none of you depose Yazid, nor let any of you go to excess in this matter, lest there be a separation between me and him.'" [Al-Musnad (2/48)]

The raised (marfu') portion of this is in the Two Sahihs.

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid related to us, Hajjaj related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, from his father, from Hudhayfah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever stipulates a condition to his brother and does not intend to fulfill it for him, is like one who lowers his neighbor into a place without protection." [Al-Musnad (5/404)]

* *

His words ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾ are a warning and threat to whoever breaks oaths after their confirmation.

* *

His words ﴿And do not be like the one who unravels her yarn after it was strong, into pieces﴾: Abdullah ibn Kathir and al-Suddi said: this was a foolish woman in Makkah who, whenever she spun something, unraveled it after making it firm.

Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: this is a parable for one who breaks his covenant after its confirmation.

This latter view is more preponderant and apparent, and whether or not there was a woman in Makkah who unraveled her yarn does not matter.

* *

His words ﴿Ankathan [into pieces]﴾ may be an ism masdar (verbal noun): she unraveled her yarn into pieces (ankathan), i.e., unraveled. It may also be a substitute (badal) for the predicate of kana: do not be ankathan (pieces), the plural of nakth from naakith (one who breaks). Hence He said after it: ﴿Taking your oaths as deceit between you﴾, i.e., deception and trickery, ﴿that one community may be greater than another community﴾, i.e., they swear to people when they are more numerous than you so that they feel secure with you; then when the opportunity to betray them arises, you betray them. So Allah forbade that, to alert from the lesser to the greater: since He forbade betrayal in this situation, then with the ability and power to do it, He forbids it all the more.

We have already mentioned, and to Allah be praise, in Surah al-Anfal (commentary on verse 58), the story of Mu'awiyah when there was a term between him and the king of the Romans. Mu'awiyah marched toward them at the end of the term, and when it had expired while he was near their lands, he raided them while they were heedless and unaware. Amr ibn Abasah said to him: "Allahu Akbar, O Mu'awiyah, fulfillment, not treachery! I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever has a term between himself and a people, let him not untie a knot until its period has ended.'" So Mu'awiyah returned with the army, may Allah be pleased with him and content him.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿that one community may be greater than another community﴾ means: more numerous.

Mujahid said: They would make alliances with allies, then find others more numerous and mightier than them, so they would break the alliance with these and ally with those who were more numerous and mightier. They were forbidden from that. Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said something similar.

* *

His words ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: meaning by the multitude. Reported by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Jarir said: that is, by His command to you to fulfill pledges and covenants.

﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ﴾, so He will recompense every doer for his deed, good or evil.

This is commanded by God Most High: fulfilling covenants and pledges, and maintaining firm oaths. Hence He said: ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾.

There is no contradiction between this and His words: ﴿And do not make Allah the target of your oaths [to be] righteous and mindful of Allah and to make peace between people﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 224], and His words: ﴿That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. And guard your oaths﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 89], meaning: do not leave them without expiation; and His words, peace be upon him, in what is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "By Allah, if Allah wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I do what is better and make expiation for my oath." And in another narration: "and I expiate for my oath." There is no contradiction among all of these, nor between them and the aforementioned verse, ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation, and you have made Allah your surety﴾, because these oaths meant are those included in covenants and pledges, not the oaths that are given to urge or to prevent. Hence Mujahid said regarding His words ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾: it means the alliance, i.e., the alliances of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period). This is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abdullah ibn Muhammad, that is Ibn Abi Shaybah, related to us: Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah related to us, from Zakariyya, that is Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance existed in the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased it in firmness."

Muslim also narrated it similarly from Ibn Abi Shaybah.

Its meaning is that in Islam there is no need for the alliance that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to make, for adherence to Islam is sufficient in place of what they were in.

As for what is reported in the Two Sahihs, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made an alliance between the Muhajirun and the Ansar in our house" — its meaning is that he established brotherhood between them, so they would inherit from one another by it, until Allah abrogated that. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi related to me, Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, Ibn Abi Layla informed us, from Muzayyidah [in another copy: Buraydah], concerning His words ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have covenanted﴾, he said: it was revealed concerning the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ). Whoever embraced Islam pledged allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ) upon Islam, so He said: ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have covenanted﴾ — this is the pledge you pledged upon Islam; ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ — the pledge. Let not the fewness of Muhammad [and his companions] and the multitude of the polytheists lead you to break the pledge you made upon Islam.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il related to us, Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi', who said: When the people deposed Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, Ibn Umar gathered his sons and family, then he recited the tashahhud, then said: "To proceed: we have pledged allegiance to this man upon the pledge of Allah and His Messenger, and I have heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, the treacherous one will have a banner raised for him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so. And among the greatest treachery—except associating partners with Allah—is that a man pledges allegiance to a man upon the pledge of Allah and His Messenger, then breaks his pledge. So let none of you depose Yazid, nor let any of you go to excess in this matter, lest there be a separation between me and him.'" [Al-Musnad (2/48)]

The raised (marfu') portion of this is in the Two Sahihs.

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid related to us, Hajjaj related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, from his father, from Hudhayfah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever stipulates a condition to his brother and does not intend to fulfill it for him, is like one who lowers his neighbor into a place without protection." [Al-Musnad (5/404)]

* *

His words ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾ are a warning and threat to whoever breaks oaths after their confirmation.

* *

His words ﴿And do not be like the one who unravels her yarn after it was strong, into pieces﴾: Abdullah ibn Kathir and al-Suddi said: this was a foolish woman in Makkah who, whenever she spun something, unraveled it after making it firm.

Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: this is a parable for one who breaks his covenant after its confirmation.

This latter view is more preponderant and apparent, and whether or not there was a woman in Makkah who unraveled her yarn does not matter.

* *

His words ﴿Ankathan [into pieces]﴾ may be an ism masdar (verbal noun): she unraveled her yarn into pieces (ankathan), i.e., unraveled. It may also be a substitute (badal) for the predicate of kana: do not be ankathan (pieces), the plural of nakth from naakith (one who breaks). Hence He said after it: ﴿Taking your oaths as deceit between you﴾, i.e., deception and trickery, ﴿that one community may be greater than another community﴾, i.e., they swear to people when they are more numerous than you so that they feel secure with you; then when the opportunity to betray them arises, you betray them. So Allah forbade that, to alert from the lesser to the greater: since He forbade betrayal in this situation, then with the ability and power to do it, He forbids it all the more.

We have already mentioned, and to Allah be praise, in Surah al-Anfal (commentary on verse 58), the story of Mu'awiyah when there was a term between him and the king of the Romans. Mu'awiyah marched toward them at the end of the term, and when it had expired while he was near their lands, he raided them while they were heedless and unaware. Amr ibn Abasah said to him: "Allahu Akbar, O Mu'awiyah, fulfillment, not treachery! I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever has a term between himself and a people, let him not untie a knot until its period has ended.'" So Mu'awiyah returned with the army, may Allah be pleased with him and content him.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿that one community may be greater than another community﴾ means: more numerous.

Mujahid said: They would make alliances with allies, then find others more numerous and mightier than them, so they would break the alliance with these and ally with those who were more numerous and mightier. They were forbidden from that. Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said something similar.

* *

His words ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: meaning by the multitude. Reported by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Jarir said: that is, by His command to you to fulfill pledges and covenants.

﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ﴾, so He will recompense every doer for his deed, good or evil.

"Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you﴾, O people, ﴿one nation﴾, as He said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [Yunus: 99], meaning: He would have brought you into agreement. And since He made [them] differ, [there is] no hatred or animosity [among them]. ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one nation, but they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them﴾ [Hud: 118, 119]. Likewise He says here: ﴿But Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾, then He will question you on the Day of Resurrection about all your deeds, and will repay you for them, down to the fetiil (the thread in a date-stone), the naqir (the speck on a date-stone), and the qitmir (the thin skin around a date-stone).

Then Allah warned His servants against taking oaths as a means of deception (dakhal), meaning treachery and deceit, lest a foot slip after it has been firmly planted. It is a parable for one who was upon uprightness, then deviated from it and strayed from the path of guidance, because of oaths that are broken, which involve turning people away from the way of Allah. For when the disbeliever sees that a believer has made a pledge to him and then betrayed him, no trust in the religion remains for him, and so he is turned away from entering Islam because of it. Therefore He said: ﴿And you would taste evil for having averted [others] from the way of Allah, and for you is a great punishment﴾.

Then Allah said: ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price﴾, meaning: do not trade faith in Allah for the goods of this worldly life and its adornment, for they are little. Even if the whole world were gathered for the son of Adam, what is with Allah would be better for him, meaning: the reward and recompense of Allah are better for whoever hopes for it, believes in Him, seeks Him, and keeps His covenant in hope of His promise. Therefore He said: ﴿If you only knew, what is with you will be exhausted﴾,

meaning: it will run out and come to an end, for it is until a counted, limited, determined, finite term. ﴿But what is with Allah is lasting﴾, meaning: His reward for you in Paradise is lasting, with no cutting off and no exhaustion, for it is everlasting, neither changing nor passing away. ﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient with their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾. This is an oath from the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, introduced with the lam of emphasis, that He will recompense the patient for their best deeds, meaning: and He will overlook their bad ones.

This is a promise from Allah, exalted is He, to whoever does righteous deeds, meaning deeds that follow the Book of Allah, exalted is He, and the Sunnah of His Prophet [[In (ت): "rasulihi" (His Messenger)]], whether male or female among the children of Adam, while their heart is a believer in Allah and His Messenger. This commanded deed is legislated by Allah, with the promise that Allah will grant them a good life in this world and will reward them with the best of what they did in the Hereafter.

The "good life" (al-hayah al-tayyibah) encompasses every aspect of comfort, from whatever direction it may come. It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of scholars that they interpreted it as lawful, good provision (al-rizq al-halal al-tayyib).

From 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, it is narrated that he interpreted it as contentment (al-qana'ah). Ibn 'Abbas said the same, as did 'Ikrimah and Wahb ibn Munabbih.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is happiness (al-sa'adah).

Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah said: No one's life is truly good except in Paradise.

Al-Dahhak said: It is lawful provision and worship in this world. Al-Dahhak also said: It is acting in obedience and finding joy in it [[In (ت، ف): "huwa" (it is)]].

The correct view is that the good life includes all of this, as in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Shurahbil ibn Shurayk narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has embraced Islam, has been given sustenance sufficient for his needs, and Allah has made him content with what He has given him, has indeed succeeded."

Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' with the same wording [[Al-Musnad (2/168) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1054).]].

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated, from the hadith of Abu Hani', from Abu 'Ali al-Janbi [[In (ت، ف، أ): "al-Hasbi"]], from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever has been guided to Islam, whose livelihood is sufficient for him, and who is content with it, has indeed succeeded." Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih hadith [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2349).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Yahya, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not wrong a believer. A good deed of his is given to him in this world, and he is rewarded for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is given his good deeds in this world, until when he reaches the Hereafter, he has no good deed for which he is given anything good." Muslim alone narrated it [[Al-Musnad (3/123) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2818).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verse 98–100:

This is a command from Allah, the Exalted, to His servants, delivered through the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ): when they intend to recite the Qur'an, they should seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. It is a recommendation (amr nadb), not an obligation (wajib). Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir and other imams reported the consensus (ijma') on this. We have already presented the hadiths concerning seeking refuge in full at the beginning of the tafsir, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

The purpose of seeking refuge at the beginning of recitation is so that the reader's recitation is not confused for him and does not become muddled, and so that it does not prevent him from reflection (tadabbur) and contemplation (tafakkur). For this reason, the majority (jumhur) held that seeking refuge comes before the recitation. It is related from Hamzah and Abu Hatim al-Sijistani that it comes after the recitation, and they used this verse as evidence. Al-Nawawi, in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab, related something similar from Abu Hurayrah as well, and from Muhammad ibn Sirin and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. The correct view is the first, because of the hadiths mentioned earlier that indicate it precedes the recitation. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾. Al-Thawri said: He has no authority over them to cause them to fall into a sin from which they do not repent.

Others said: its meaning is that he has no proof against them. Others said: it is like His saying: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [Sad: 83].

﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾. Mujahid said: those who obey him.

Others said: those who take him as a protector apart from Allah.

﴿And those who associate others with Him﴾: that is, they associate partners in the worship of Allah, the Exalted. It is possible that the "ba'" here is causal (sababiyyah), meaning: they became polytheists with Allah, the Exalted, because of their obedience to Satan.

Others said: its meaning is that he became their partner in wealth and children.

Mujahid said: ﴿When We substitute a verse in place of another verse﴾ means: We lift it and establish another in its place.

Qatadah said: it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106].

Then Allah, exalted is He, responded to them, saying: ﴿Say: The Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus, i.e. Jibril) has brought it down from your Lord in truth﴾, meaning with truthfulness and justice, ﴿to strengthen those who believe﴾, so that they affirm what was revealed first and second, and their hearts are humbled before it, ﴿and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims﴾, meaning He made it a guide [giving guidance] and a glad tiding for the Muslims who believed in Allah and His messengers.

Allah says, informing about the polytheists and what they used to say of falsehood, fabrication and slander: that Muhammad is only being taught this Qur'an that he recites to us by a human being. They point to a foreign (a'jami) man who was among them, a slave belonging to some of the clans of Quraysh, who was a seller who sold at as-Safa. Sometimes the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would sit with him and speak with him a little. That man was a non-Arabic speaker who did not know Arabic, or he knew a little of it, just enough to return replies to the disputants in what was necessary. Therefore Allah the Exalted said, refuting them in their fabrication: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. That is, how could one who brought this Qur'an, with its eloquence, its rhetoric and its complete, all-encompassing meanings, which are more perfect than the meanings of every book sent down to any prophet who was sent, learn from a foreign man?! Only someone with no trace of intellect would say this.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in as-Sirah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as far as I have been informed, often sat near al-Marwah beside the stall of a Christian slave called Jabr, a slave of some of the Banu al-Hadrami. [They would say: "By Allah, Muhammad is not taught much of what he brings except by Jabr the Christian, the slave of the Banu al-Hadrami."] Then Allah revealed: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue﴾. [Reference: as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/393).]

Similarly, Abdullah ibn Kathir said: and from Ikrimah and Qatadah: his name was Ya'ish.

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad at-Tusi narrated to me, Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Abdullah al-Mula'i, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach a smith in Makkah, whose name was Balgham, and he was non-Arabic speaking. The polytheists would see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entering to him and leaving from his presence, and they said: "He is only being taught by Balgham." So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue﴾. [Tafsir at-Tabari (14/119).]

Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: he was Salman al-Farisi, but this view is weak, because this verse is Meccan, and Salman only embraced Islam in Madinah.

Ubayd Allah ibn Muslim said: We had two Roman slaves who would read a book of theirs in their own language, and the Prophet ﷺ would pass by them, stop and listen to them. The polytheists said: "He is learning from them," so Allah revealed this verse.

Az-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, said: The one among the polytheists who said that was a man who used to write the revelation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he apostatized from Islam afterward and fabricated this statement. May Allah disfigure him!

He, exalted is He, informs us that He does not guide those who turn away from His remembrance and neglect what He has sent down to His Messenger, and who have no intention of believing in what has come from Allah. This category of people, Allah does not guide to faith in His signs and in what He sent His messengers with in this world, and for them there is a painful, agonizing torment in the Hereafter.

Then He informs us that His Messenger is neither a fabricator nor a liar, because ﴿Only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah fabricate lies﴾ against Allah and against His Messenger. They are the most evil of creation: disbelievers and deviators, known among people for lying. The Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) was the most truthful, most righteous, and most complete of people in knowledge, action, faith, and certainty, known for truthfulness among his people. None of them doubted this, to the extent that he was called by no name among them except "the Trustworthy, Muhammad."

This is why, when Hiraql (Heraclius), king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan about those questions he asked concerning the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among what he said to him was: "Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" He replied: "No." Hiraql said: "Then he would not leave off lying about people only to go and lie about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 16, verses 106–109:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about those who disbelieve in Him after having faith and clear insight, and who open their breasts to disbelief and are content with it: that He has become angry with them, because of their knowledge of faith and then their turning away from it, and that for them there is a great punishment in the Hereafter. This is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, so they proceeded to what they proceeded to of apostasy (riddah) for the sake of the world, and Allah did not guide their hearts or make them firm upon the true religion. Therefore He sealed upon their hearts, so they do not understand anything by them that would benefit them, and He sealed upon their hearing and their sight, so they do not benefit by them, and they were of no avail to them in anything. So they are heedless of what is intended for them.

﴿Without doubt﴾, that is: it is necessary, and it is no wonder, that whoever has this description, ﴿in the Hereafter they are the losers﴾, that is, those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

As for His saying: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart is secure in faith﴾, it is an exception from the one who disbelieved with his tongue, agreeing with the polytheists verbally under compulsion because of the beating and harm he suffered, while his heart refuses what he says, and he is secure in faith in Allah and His Messenger.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that this verse was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, when the polytheists tortured him until he disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), so he agreed with them in that under compulsion, and came apologising to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse. Likewise said ash-Sha'bi, Abu Malik and Qatadah.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Abu 'Ubaydah [ibn] Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The polytheists seized 'Ammar ibn Yasir and tortured him until he came close to them in some of what they wanted. He complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "How do you find your heart?" He said: "Secure in faith." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If they return, then return."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in a fuller form, and in it he cursed the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned their gods with praise, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was not left alone until I reviled you and mentioned their gods with praise!" He said: "How do you find your heart?" He said: "Secure in faith." He said: "If they return, then return." And concerning that Allah revealed: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart is secure in faith﴾.

For this reason the scholars agreed that it is permissible for one who is compelled to disbelief to comply, to preserve his life, and it is permissible for him to resist to the death, as Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) refused them while they did terrible things to him, so much so that they would place a great rock on his chest in intense heat and order him to associate partners with Allah, and he refused them, saying: "One, One." And he would say: "By Allah, if I knew a word that angered you more than this, I would say it." May Allah be pleased with him and content him. Likewise Habib ibn Zayd al-Ansari, when Musaylimah the Liar said to him: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "Yes." He said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "I do not hear." So he kept cutting him into pieces, piece by piece, while he remained steadfast in that.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il related to us, Ayyub related to us, from 'Ikrimah, that 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) burned some people who had apostatised from Islam. This reached Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I would not have burned them with fire, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not punish with the punishment of Allah.' And I would have killed them, according to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him.'" This reached 'Ali, who said: "Woe to the mother of Ibn 'Abbas!" Al-Bukhari narrated it.

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal al-'Adawi, from Abu Burdah, who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal came to Abu Musa in Yemen, and there was a man with him. He said: "What is this?" He said: "A man who was a Jew, then became Muslim, then reverted to Judaism, and we have been seeking to bring him back to Islam for, I think, two months." He said: "By Allah, I will not sit down until you strike his neck." So his neck was struck. Then he said: "Allah and His Messenger have decreed that whoever turns back from his religion, kill him," or he said: "Whoever changes his religion, kill him."

This story is in the two Sahihs with different wording.

The better and more excellent course is that the Muslim remain firm upon his religion, even if it leads to his death, as al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in the biography of 'Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi, one of the Companions: that the Romans captured him and brought him to their king, who said to him: "Become a Christian, and I will share my kingdom with you and marry you to my daughter." He said to him: "Even if you gave me all that you possess and all that the Arabs possess, on condition that I abandon the religion of Muhammad for the blink of an eye, I would not do it!" He said: "Then I will kill you." He said: "You and that!" So he ordered him to be crucified, and ordered archers to shoot near his hands and feet, while he was presented with the religion of Christianity and refused it. Then he ordered him to be taken down, and ordered a cauldron. In another narration: a brass cow, which was heated, and he brought a Muslim captive and threw him in while he watched, and there were only bones showing. He presented it to him and he refused, so he ordered that he be thrown in. He was raised on a pulley to be thrown in, and he wept. The king hoped for him and called him and said: "I only wept because my soul is only one soul, which will be thrown into this cauldron now for God's sake, and I wished that I had a soul for every hair on my body to be tortured this torment for God's sake." In some narrations: he imprisoned him, withheld food and drink from him for days, then sent him wine and pork, and he did not approach it. Then he summoned him and said: "What prevented you from eating?" He said: "As for it, it had become lawful to me, but I would not give you the satisfaction of seeing me." The king said to him: "Then kiss my head and I will release you." He said: "And will you release with me all the Muslim captives?" He said: "Yes." So he kissed his head, and he released him and released with him all the Muslim captives who were with him. When he returned, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "It is a right upon every Muslim to kiss the head of 'Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah, and I will begin." He stood and kissed his head.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in a fuller form, and in it he cursed the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned their gods with praise, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was not left alone until I reviled you and mentioned their gods with praise!" He said: "How do you find your heart?" He said: "Secure in faith." He said: "If they return, then return." And concerning that Allah revealed: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart is secure in faith﴾.

For this reason the scholars agreed that it is permissible for one who is compelled to disbelief to comply, to preserve his life, and it is permissible for him to resist to the death, as Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) refused them while they did terrible things to him, so much so that they would place a great rock on his chest in intense heat and order him to associate partners with Allah, and he refused them, saying: "One, One." And he would say: "By Allah, if I knew a word that angered you more than this, I would say it." May Allah be pleased with him and content him. Likewise Habib ibn Zayd al-Ansari, when Musaylimah the Liar said to him: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "Yes." He said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "I do not hear." So he kept cutting him into pieces, piece by piece, while he remained steadfast in that.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il related to us, Ayyub related to us, from 'Ikrimah, that 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) burned some people who had apostatised from Islam. This reached Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I would not have burned them with fire, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not punish with the punishment of Allah.' And I would have killed them, according to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him.'" This reached 'Ali, who said: "Woe to the mother of Ibn 'Abbas!" Al-Bukhari narrated it.

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal al-'Adawi, from Abu Burdah, who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal came to Abu Musa in Yemen, and there was a man with him. He said: "What is this?" He said: "A man who was a Jew, then became Muslim, then reverted to Judaism, and we have been seeking to bring him back to Islam for, I think, two months." He said: "By Allah, I will not sit down until you strike his neck." So his neck was struck. Then he said: "Allah and His Messenger have decreed that whoever turns back from his religion, kill him," or he said: "Whoever changes his religion, kill him."

This story is in the two Sahihs with different wording.

The better and more excellent course is that the Muslim remain firm upon his religion, even if it leads to his death, as al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in the biography of 'Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi, one of the Companions: that the Romans captured him and brought him to their king, who said to him: "Become a Christian, and I will share my kingdom with you and marry you to my daughter." He said to him: "Even if you gave me all that you possess and all that the Arabs possess, on condition that I abandon the religion of Muhammad for the blink of an eye, I would not do it!" He said: "Then I will kill you." He said: "You and that!" So he ordered him to be crucified, and ordered archers to shoot near his hands and feet, while he was presented with the religion of Christianity and refused it. Then he ordered him to be taken down, and ordered a cauldron. In another narration: a brass cow, which was heated, and he brought a Muslim captive and threw him in while he watched, and there were only bones showing. He presented it to him and he refused, so he ordered that he be thrown in. He was raised on a pulley to be thrown in, and he wept. The king hoped for him and called him and said: "I only wept because my soul is only one soul, which will be thrown into this cauldron now for God's sake, and I wished that I had a soul for every hair on my body to be tortured this torment for God's sake." In some narrations: he imprisoned him, withheld food and drink from him for days, then sent him wine and pork, and he did not approach it. Then he summoned him and said: "What prevented you from eating?" He said: "As for it, it had become lawful to me, but I would not give you the satisfaction of seeing me." The king said to him: "Then kiss my head and I will release you." He said: "And will you release with me all the Muslim captives?" He said: "Yes." So he kissed his head, and he released him and released with him all the Muslim captives who were with him. When he returned, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "It is a right upon every Muslim to kiss the head of 'Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah, and I will begin." He stood and kissed his head.

These are another group, who were oppressed in Makkah and humiliated among their people, and who had acquiesced to the trial (fitnah). Then Allah made deliverance possible for them through emigration (hijrah), so they left their lands, their families and their wealth, seeking the good pleasure of Allah (ridwan Allah) and His forgiveness. They joined the ranks of the believers, fought alongside them against the disbelievers, and were patient. So Allah the Exalted informed that He is, ﴿after that﴾, i.e., after that deed, which is their yielding to the trial, ﴿Forgiving toward them, Merciful to them on the Day of their return.﴾

﴿On the Day when every soul will come pleading for itself﴾, i.e., arguing (tuhajju) ﴿on its own behalf﴾. No one will argue on its behalf: neither a father, nor a son, nor a brother, nor a wife. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, i.e., of good and evil, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, i.e., the reward of good will not be diminished, nor will the recompense for evil be increased, and they will not be wronged even by the size of a naqir [[In T: "the one who does evil" (al-musi').]].

This is a parable struck for the people of Makkah. It was a secure, tranquil and settled city, while people were snatched away from around it, and whoever entered it was safe and had nothing to fear. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They said, "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land." Did We not establish for them a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of all things are brought as provision from Us?﴾ [al-Qasas: 57]. Likewise, here He says: ﴿Its provision came to it in abundance from every place﴾, meaning its sustenance came easily and pleasantly. ﴿But it denied the favours of Allah﴾, meaning it rejected the blessings of Allah upon it. The greatest of these was the sending of Muhammad ﷺ to them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin? Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the place of settling﴾ [Ibrahim: 28-29]. For this reason Allah replaced their former state with its opposite, and He said: ﴿So Allah made it taste the clothing of hunger and fear﴾, meaning He clothed it in and made it taste hunger, after it had been that the fruits of all things were brought to them and their provision came to them in abundance from every place. This happened when they defied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and refused anything but opposition to him. So he invoked against them with seven years of drought like the seven years of Yusuf (Joseph), and a devastating year struck them that destroyed everything they had. They ate al-'Ilhiz, which is the wool of a camel mixed with its blood when they slaughtered it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and fear﴾: this is because they were given fear in place of their security, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions, when they migrated to Madinah, fearing the assault of his raiding parties and armies. Everything they owned was in ruin and destruction, until Allah granted him victory over them. This was because of their conduct, their transgression and their denial of the Messenger whom Allah sent among them, one of themselves, and with whom He showed favour to them in His saying: ﴿Allah certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164]. He also says: ﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a reminder, a messenger who recites to you the verses of Allah as clear evidence, that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darkness into light﴾ [al-Talaq: 10-11] and so on, and His saying: ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you what you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151-152].

Just as their condition was reversed upon the disbelievers, so that they feared after security and went hungry after plenty, Allah replaced the fear of the believers with security, gave them provision after poverty, and made them the leaders of the people, their rulers, their masters, their commanders and their imams.

This is what we have said, that this parable was struck for Makkah. It was related by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid, Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam also held this view, and Malik related it from al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy on them all.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Nafi' ibn Zayd narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh narrated to us, that Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith al-Hadrami narrated to him that he heard Mishrah ibn Ha'an say: I heard Sulaym ibn Itr say: We returned from Hajj with Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, while Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, was besieged in Madinah. She kept asking about him: "What has happened?" until she saw two riders, and she sent to them asking them. They said: "He has been killed." Hafsah said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, this is the town of which Allah said: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah﴾." Abu Shurayh said: Ubayd Allah ibn al-Mughirah informed me, from someone who narrated to him, that he used to say: "It is Madinah."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/125).]

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His believing servants to eat of His lawful and good provision and to be thankful to Him for it, for He is the One who bestows favour and grace upon them from the outset, the One who alone deserves worship with no partner.

Then He mentioned what He has forbidden to them, which is harmful to them in their religion and their worldly life: carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine.

﴿And that over which other than Allah has been invoked﴾, meaning slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾, meaning forced by necessity, ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing﴾, ﴿indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

The discussion of a verse like this has already been presented in Surat al-Baqarah (at the commentary on verse 137), sufficient to not repeat it here, and all praise and grace belong to Allah.

Then the Exalted forbade following the way of the polytheists, who declared things lawful and unlawful merely by what they had devised and agreed upon among names by their own opinions, such as the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, the waṣīlah and the ḥām, and other things that they had made into law for themselves, innovating them in their time of ignorance (jāhiliyyah). So He said:

﴿And do not say, regarding what your tongues falsely describe, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood against Allah.﴾

This applies to everyone who innovates an innovation for which he has no legitimate basis in the Sharia, or who makes lawful something Allah has forbidden, or forbids something Allah has permitted, merely by his own opinion and whim.

The "mā" in His saying ﴿lima﴾ is a verbal (maṣdariyyah) particle, meaning: "And do not say falsehood by the description of your tongues."

Then He threatened for this, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed.﴾ That is, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. As for this world, it is a little enjoyment; as for the Hereafter, theirs is a painful punishment. As He said: ﴿We will give them enjoyment for a little, then We will drive them to a harsh punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24], and He said: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed. [It is] an enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 69–70].

When He mentioned that He had only forbidden us carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that He had granted a concession regarding it in cases of necessity (and in that there is ease for this Ummah, for whom Allah desires ease and does not desire hardship), He, glory be to Him, mentioned what He had forbidden to the Jews in their law before abrogating it, and the burdens, shackles, hardship and constraint they were under. He said: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade what We have related to you before﴾, meaning in Surat al-An'am, in His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with undivided hoofs; and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs or entrails carry or what is mixed with bone. That was their recompense for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful﴾ [al-An'am: 146]. Therefore He said here: ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾, meaning in what We restricted for them, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾, meaning they deserved that. As He said: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them and for their averting from the way of Allah many times over﴾ [an-Nisa': 160].

Then Allah, out of generosity and grace toward the disobedient believers, informed that whoever of them repents to Him, He will accept his repentance. He said: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who did evil in ignorance﴾. Some of the early scholars (salaf) said: Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant.

﴿Then repent after that and reform﴾, meaning they give up the sins they were engaged in and turn to performing acts of obedience. ﴿Indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning after that deed and that wrongdoing.

Ibn Kathir praises Allah's servant, messenger and close friend (khalil) Ibrahim (Abraham), the leader of the ḥunafa' (those who turn away from false religions to pure monotheism) and father of the prophets, and clears him of the polytheists, and of Judaism and Christianity. So He says: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth (ḥanīf), and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ As for "ummah" (nation), it means the leader who is followed. And "qānit" means the humble and obedient. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 16, verse 124:

There is no doubt that God, exalted is He, prescribed for every religious community (milla) a day of the week on which people gather for worship. God prescribed for this community the day of Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah), because it is the sixth day on which God completed creation, and on which people gather and God's blessing upon His servants was completed. It is said that God prescribed this for the Children of Israel through the tongue of Moses, but they deviated from it and chose Saturday (al-Sabt), because it is the day on which the Lord created none of the creatures whose creation He had completed on Friday. So God obligated them to it in the Law of the Torah, and charged them to hold fast to it and to observe it, along with His command to them to follow Muhammad (ﷺ) when He sent him. And He took their covenants and pledges upon that. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Sabbath was only prescribed for those who differed concerning it﴾.

Mujahid said: They followed it and abandoned Friday.

Then they continued to hold firmly to it until God sent 'Isa (Jesus) son of Maryam. It is said that he turned them to Sunday (Yawm al-Ahad). It is also said that he did not abandon the Law of the Torah except for what was abrogated (naskh) of some of its rulings, and that he continued to observe Saturday until he was raised up. And that the Christians after him, in the time of Constantine (Qustantin), were the ones who shifted to Sunday, in opposition to the Jews, and shifted to praying facing east away from the Rock. And God knows best.

It is firmly established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "We are the last but first on the Day of Resurrection, though they were given the Book before us. Then this is their day which God made obligatory upon them, but they differed concerning it, so God guided us to it. So people are followers of us in it: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow." This is the wording of al-Bukhari.

And from Abu Hurayrah and Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God led astray from Friday those who were before us. For the Jews there was the day of Saturday, and for the Christians there was the day of Sunday. Then God brought us and guided us to Friday, so He made Friday, Saturday and Sunday [in order]; and likewise they are followers of us on the Day of Resurrection. We are the last of the people of the world and the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the matter will be judged between them before all creatures." Narrated by Muslim. [And God knows best.]

Allah says, commanding His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to call the creation to Allah **"with wisdom"** (al-hikmah).

Ibn Jarir said: It is what He revealed to him (in the manuscripts f and a: "to you") of the Book and the Sunnah. **"And with good admonition"** (al-mawizah al-hasanah), meaning: with what it contains of warnings and accounts of the events that befell people, by which he reminds them, so that they may beware of the punishment (ba's) of Allah, the Exalted.

* *

As for His saying: **"And argue with them in the best manner"** (wa jadilhum billati hiya ahsan), meaning: whoever among them needs debate and disputation, let it be in the best manner, with gentleness, softness and good speech, as He said: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 46]. So Allah commanded him to be gentle, just as He commanded Musa and Harun, peace be upon them, when He sent them to Fir'awn, saying: ﴿So speak to him with gentle speech; perhaps he will be reminded or fear﴾ [Ta-Ha: 44].

* *

As for His saying: **"Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided"**, meaning: He has already decreed the knowledge of who among them is wretched and who is happy, and He has written that and completed it. So call them to Allah, and do not let your soul waste away in grief over those among them who have gone astray. Indeed, it is not upon you to guide them; you are only a warner, and upon you is only the conveying (of the message), and upon Us is the reckoning. ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like﴾ [Al-Qasas: 56], and ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 272].

Allah commands justice in retaliation and equivalence in exacting one's right, as ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Khalid, from Ibn Sirin, that he said concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So retaliate against them with the same as that with which you were afflicted﴾: "If a man takes something from you, then take from him the like of it."

Likewise said Mujahid, Ibrahim, al-Hasan al-Basri, and others. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view.

Ibn Zayd said: They had been commanded to forgive the polytheists. Then some men of strength and standing embraced Islam and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if Allah permitted us, we would take revenge on these dogs!" So this verse was revealed, and then that was abrogated (naskh) by the command to fight (jihad).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from some of his companions, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, who said: The whole of Surah al-Nahl was revealed in Makkah, except three verses at its end, which were revealed in Madinah after Uhud, when Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed and mutilated. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If we gain victory over them, we will mutilate thirty men from among them." When the Muslims heard that, they said: "By Allah, if we gain victory over them, we will mutilate them with a mutilation such as no one among the Arabs has ever inflicted on anyone." So Allah revealed: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted﴾ to the end of the surah. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/132).]

This report is mursal, and in its chain there is an unnamed man (rajul mubham). This has been narrated through another, connected route. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn ʿAsim narrated to us, Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu ʿUthman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood over Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was martyred, and he looked upon a sight that was more painful to the heart than any he had seen. Or he said: "to his heart." Then he looked at him, and he had been mutilated, and he said: "May the mercy of Allah be upon you. You were, as far as I know, one who kept ties of kinship and did many good deeds. By Allah, were it not for the grief of those after you over you, I would have been pleased to leave you until Allah raises you from the bellies of beasts of prey, or a word similar to that. Truly, by Allah, in return for that, I will mutilate seventy of them as you have been mutilated." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, descended upon Muhammad (ﷺ) with this surah and recited: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted﴾ to the end of the verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expiated for his oath (meaning, from his right hand) and refrained from that.

[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1795, Kashf al-Astar.]

This chain is weak, because Salih (who is Ibn Bashir al-Murri) is weak according to the imams, and al-Bukhari said: he is munkar al-hadith (one whose narrations are rejected).

Al-Sha'bi and Ibn Juraij said: It was revealed concerning the words of the Muslims on the day of Uhud regarding those who had been mutilated: "We will mutilate them." So Allah revealed this concerning them.

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of his father: Hadiyyah ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, ʿIsa ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: When the day of Uhud came, sixty men from the Ansar were killed, and six from the Muhajirun. The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If we ever have a day like this against the polytheists, we will surpass them in retaliation." Then, when the day of the Conquest came, a man said: "Quraysh will not be recognized after today." A caller proclaimed: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has granted security to black and white alike, except for so-and-so and so-and-so" (naming people). So Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿And if you punish, [then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient]﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said: "We will be patient and will not punish."

[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/135).]

This noble verse has parallels in the Qur'an, for it contains the legitimacy of justice and the encouragement toward excellence, as in His words: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it; but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. And He said: ﴿And for wounds is legal retribution; but whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45]. And in this noble verse He said: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted﴾, then said: ﴿But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾.

* *

His words: ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾ are an emphasis on the command to patience, and an informing that it is attained only by the will of Allah, His help, and His power.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾, i.e., over those who oppose you; do not grieve over them, for Allah has decreed that. ﴿And do not be in distress﴾, i.e., in grief, ﴿over what they plot﴾, i.e., over what they exert themselves in enmity toward you and in bringing evil upon you. Indeed, Allah is sufficient for you, your helper, your supporter, and He will make you victorious over them.

* *

His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾, i.e., He is with them by His support, His help, and His aid. This is a special companionship, like His words: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12], and His words to Musa and Harun: ﴿Fear not; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46], and the Prophet's (ﷺ) words to the Siddiq while they were in the cave: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40]. As for the general companionship, it is by hearing, seeing, and knowledge, as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are; and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Hadid: 4], and as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? There is no private conversation among three but that He is their fourth, nor among five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7], and as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you are not in any matter, nor recite of it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but that We are witnesses over you when you are involved therein. And not absent from your Lord is any weight of an atom within the earth or within the heaven or anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear register﴾ [Yunus: 61].
